title.zh: 卷三百七十九 列傳第一百三十八 章誼 韓肖冑 陳公輔 張觷 胡松年 曹勛 李稙 韓公裔
title.en: Volume 379 Biographies 138: Zhang Yi, Han Xiaozhou, Chen Gongfu, Zhang Xue, Hu Songnian, Cao Xun, Li Zhi, Han Gongyi
title.raw: 卷三百七十九 列傳第一百三十八 章誼 韓肖冑 陳公輔 張觷 胡松年 曹勛 李稙 韓公裔 Volume 379 Biographies 138: Zhang Yi, Han Xiaozhou, Chen Gongfu, Zhang Xue, Hu Songnian, Cao Xun, Li Zhi, Han Gongyi

sentences.zh: 章誼，字宜叟，建州浦城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Yishou, was a native of Pucheng in Jian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi, whose courtesy name was Yishou, came from Pucheng in Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 登崇寧四年進士第，補懷州司法參軍，歷漳、台二州教授、杭州通判。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of the Chongning era, was appointed judicial aide in Huai prefecture, and served successively as instructor in Zhang and Tai prefectures and as vice-prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in 1105, took up a post as judicial aide in Huaizhou, and later served as instructor in both Zhangzhou and Taizhou before becoming vice-prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，陳通寇錢塘，城閉，部使者檄誼聚杭州七縣弓兵，以張聲勢。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyan era, Chen Tong raided Qiantang; the city gates were shut, and the circuit commissioner ordered Zhang Yi to gather bow troops from the seven counties of Hangzhou to make a show of force.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyan reign, the bandit Chen Tong attacked the Hangzhou area; with the city sealed off, the regional commissioner ordered Zhang Yi to muster archer militia from Hangzhou's seven counties to swell the appearance of strength.

sentences.zh: 會王淵討賊，誼隨淵得入城，賊平，旋加撫定，人皆德之。

translations.literal: When Wang Yuan came to suppress the bandits, Zhang Yi followed Yuan and was able to enter the city; after the rebels were pacified, he was soon charged with securing the area, and everyone praised his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuan arrived to crush the rebels; Zhang Yi accompanied him into the city. Once order was restored, Yi was put in charge of reassurance work, and the people credited him with their deliverance.

sentences.zh: 帝幸臨安，苗、劉為變，帝御樓，宰臣百執事咸在，人心恟恟。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to Lin'an, Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan staged a mutiny; the emperor ascended the tower, and the chief ministers and all officials were present; popular sentiment was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor moved to Lin'an, Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan rose in mutiny. The emperor appeared atop the palace tower with all his chief ministers and officials in attendance while panic spread through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 帝問群臣曰：「今日之事何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the assembled ministers, "What do you make of today's events?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to his ministers and asked, "What is your judgment of what has happened today?"

sentences.zh: 浙西安撫司主管機宜文字時希孟輙曰：「乞問三軍。」

translations.literal: Shi Ximeng, handler of confidential documents in the Zhexi Pacification Commission, abruptly said, "I beg to ask the three armies."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ximeng, a confidential clerk on the Zhexi Pacification staff, spoke up at once: "I submit that Your Majesty should ask the three armies."

sentences.zh: 誼越班斥之曰：「問三軍何義？

translations.literal: Zhang Yi stepped forward out of turn and rebuked him, saying, "What is the meaning of asking the three armies?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi broke ranks and rebuked him: "What do you mean by consulting the armies?

sentences.zh: 若將鼓亂邪？」

translations.literal: Are you going to incite mutiny?"
translations.idiomatic: Are you trying to stir up a mutiny?"

sentences.zh: 希孟卻立屏息，帝嘉之。

translations.literal: Shi Ximeng withdrew and stood in silence; the emperor commended Zhang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Ximeng fell back and held his tongue. The emperor praised Zhang Yi for it.

sentences.zh: 事定，竄希孟吉陽軍，誼遷二秩，擢倉部員外郎。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Shi Ximeng was banished to Jiyang commandery; Zhang Yi was advanced two ranks and promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Once calm was restored, Ximeng was exiled to Jiyang, while Yi was raised two ranks and appointed vice director in the Revenue Ministry.

sentences.zh: 奉使二浙，貿易祠牒以濟軍用，以稽遲罷。

translations.literal: On a mission to the two Zhe circuits, he traded memorial permits to support military expenses but was dismissed for delay.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent on a mission through both Zhe circuits to exchange commemorative certificates for military funds, but lost his post for slow progress.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召為駕部員外郎，遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled as vice director in the Ministry of Ceremonies for transport and then moved to supervising censor in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was recalled to the Transport Ministry and then promoted to palace supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 張浚宣撫陝西，誼奏：「自趙哲退敗，事任已重，處斷太專，當除副貳，使之自助。」

translations.literal: When Zhang Jun was appointed pacification commissioner for Shaanxi, Zhang Yi memorialized: "Since Zhao Zhe's retreat and defeat, his responsibilities have grown weighty and his decisions too proprietary; a deputy should be appointed so he may have assistance."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun took up the Shaanxi pacification commission, Yi memorialized that since Zhao Zhe's defeat Zhang Jun's burden had grown so heavy and his discretion so absolute that a deputy should be named to share the load.

sentences.zh: 何㮚贈官，誼論其折衝無謀，守禦無策，乃中國招禍之首，乞寢免。

translations.literal: When He Li was granted a posthumous office, Zhang Yi argued that he had been without stratagem in confrontation and without plan in defense, being the foremost man to bring disaster upon the dynasty, and begged that the grant be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: When He Li was slated for a posthumous promotion, Zhang Yi argued that He had lacked both strategy in diplomacy and plans in defense—he had been chief among those who invited catastrophe on the state—and asked that the honor be set aside.

sentences.zh: 邵青自太平乘舟抵平江，所至劫掠。

translations.literal: Shao Qing sailed from Taiping to Pingjiang and plundered wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Qing sailed from Taiping to Pingjiang, looting every place he touched.

sentences.zh: 誼請置水軍於駐蹕之地，且言：「古舟師有三等，大為陣腳，次為戰船，小為傳令，皆可為戰守之備。」

translations.literal: Zhang Yi requested that a naval force be stationed at the imperial residence and said: "In antiquity there were three grades of fleet: large vessels as the battle line, next war junks, and small ones for signals—all could serve for offense and defense."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi urged posting a river navy at the imperial encampment, noting that ancient fleets had three tiers—large ships as the battle line, mid-sized war junks, and small dispatch boats—each useful for attack or defense."

sentences.zh: 詔淮南三宣撫措置。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the three Huainan pacification commissioners to arrange it.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the three Huainan pacification commissioners to carry this out.

sentences.zh: 誼又獻戰守四策，謂：「金人累歲南侵，我亦累歲奔走，蓋謀國之臣誤陛下也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi also submitted four policies for offense and defense, saying: "The Jurchens have raided south year after year, and we too have fled year after year—surely the ministers who plan for the state have misled Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi also offered four proposals on war and defense, arguing that while the Jurchens had invaded the south year after year, the court had spent those same years in flight—ministers charged with statecraft had misled the throne.

sentences.zh: 比者駐蹕揚州，有兵數十萬，可以一戰。

translations.literal: Recently, when the court halted at Yangzhou, there were several hundred thousand troops—enough for one battle.
translations.idiomatic: When the court had lately encamped at Yangzhou, it had several hundred thousand troops on hand—enough to stand and fight.

sentences.zh: 斥候不明，金人奄至，逾江而東，此宰相黃潛善、汪伯彥過也。

translations.literal: Scouts were unclear; the Jurchens arrived suddenly and crossed the river eastward—this was the fault of the chief ministers Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan.
translations.idiomatic: Because reconnaissance failed, the enemy appeared without warning and crossed the Yangzi eastward—a failure owed to Chief Councillors Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan.

sentences.zh: 前年，移蹕建康，兵練將勇，據長江之險，可守矣。

translations.literal: The year before last, when the court moved to Jiankang, the troops were trained and the generals brave; holding the Yangzi's strategic barrier, it could have been defended.
translations.idiomatic: The year before, when the court shifted to Jiankang, the army was drilled and its commanders resolute; holding the Yangzi barrier, the position was defensible.

sentences.zh: 舟師不設，二相異意，金人未至，遵海而南，此宰相呂頤浩過也。

translations.literal: No fleet was established; the two chief ministers were at odds; before the Jurchens arrived, the court fled south along the coast—this was the fault of Chief Councillor Lü Yihao.
translations.idiomatic: No river navy was organized; the two chief ministers pulled in different directions; and before the enemy even arrived the court fled south along the coast—a failure laid at Lü Yihao's door.

sentences.zh: 不知今年守戰之策安所從出？

translations.literal: I do not know from whom this year's policies of defense and offense are to come.
translations.idiomatic: Who, then, is to supply this year's strategy for holding the line or giving battle?

sentences.zh: 執政大臣誰為陛下任此事者？

translations.literal: Which of the chief ministers in power will undertake this matter for Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Which minister in power will actually shoulder this for Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂有江海，必資舟楫戰守之具；

translations.literal: This subject ventures to say that where there are rivers and seas, one must rely on vessels and equipment for naval offense and defense;
translations.idiomatic: In my view, wherever there are rivers and seas, the state must have ships and gear for naval war and defense;

sentences.zh: 有險阻，必資郡縣防守之力；

translations.literal: where there are strategic barriers, one must rely on the defensive strength of prefectures and counties;
translations.idiomatic: where there are natural barriers, it must lean on prefectures and counties for defense;

sentences.zh: 有兵將，必駕馭撫循，不可為將帥自衛之資；

translations.literal: where there are troops and generals, one must control and comfort them—they must not become resources for generals' private self-defense;
translations.idiomatic: where there are armies and commanders, the throne must govern and reassure them, not let them become private guards for their generals;

sentences.zh: 有糧賦，必漕運轉輸，不可為盜賊侵據之用。

translations.literal: where there are grain levies, one must transport them by canal—they must not become spoils for bandits to seize.
translations.idiomatic: where there is grain revenue, it must move by canal transport, not fall into bandits' hands.

sentences.zh: 四者各付能臣，分路以辦，重賞嚴罰，誰敢不用命哉！」

translations.literal: Let each of the four be entrusted to capable ministers, assigned by route to carry out, with heavy rewards and stern punishments—who would dare not obey?"
translations.idiomatic: Assign each of the four to able ministers, each with his own route and mandate, backed by rich rewards and harsh penalties—who would refuse to serve?"

sentences.zh: 詔問保民、弭盜、遏寇、生財之策，誼對曰：「去姦貪殘虐之吏，則民可保；

translations.literal: An edict asked for policies to protect the people, quell banditry, check invaders, and generate wealth; Zhang Yi replied: "Remove corrupt, greedy, and cruel officials, and the people can be protected;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor solicited plans to protect the people, suppress bandits, hold back invaders, and grow revenue. Zhang Yi answered: "Remove corrupt and brutal officials, and the people can be secured;

sentences.zh: 用循良廉平之吏，則盜可弭；

translations.literal: employ upright and fair officials, and banditry can be quelled;
translations.idiomatic: appoint upright and fair officials, and banditry will subside;

sentences.zh: 敵寇未遏，以未得折衝禦侮之臣；

translations.literal: invaders are not yet checked because we have not obtained ministers who can confront foes and repel insult;
translations.idiomatic: invaders remain unchecked because we lack ministers who can confront the enemy and repel aggression;

sentences.zh: 財賦未裕，以未得掌財心計之臣。

translations.literal: revenues are not ample because we have not obtained ministers who master finance and planning.
translations.idiomatic: treasury revenue stays thin because we lack ministers who truly understand fiscal planning.

sentences.zh: 凡此四者，任人不任法，則政治可得而治矣。」

translations.literal: In all these four matters, if one entrusts men rather than relying on statutes alone, government can be brought to order."
translations.idiomatic: On all four counts, if the throne appoints the right men rather than trusting rules alone, government can be set in order."

sentences.zh: 詔集議明堂配享，胡直儒等請合祭天地，而以太祖、太宗配。

translations.literal: An edict convened discussion on spirit tablets at the Bright Hall; Hu Zhiru and others requested joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, with Taizu and Taizong as associates.
translations.idiomatic: The court convened debate on Bright Hall spirit tablets. Hu Zhiru and others proposed a joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth with both Taizu and Taizong as associates.

sentences.zh: 誼言：「稽之經旨則未合，參之典故則未盡，施之事帝則未為簡嚴。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi said: "Checked against canonical meaning it does not accord; compared with historical precedents it is not complete; applied to the service of the Lord on High it is not concise and solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi objected: "Measured against the classics it does not fit; measured against precedent it is incomplete; applied to the worship of Heaven it is neither concise nor dignified.

sentences.zh: 今國家既以太祖配天于郊，比周之后稷，則太宗宜配帝於明堂，以比周之文王。

translations.literal: Now that the state already has Taizu accompany Heaven at the suburban altar, comparable to Hou Ji of Zhou, then Taizong should accompany the Lord at the Bright Hall, comparable to King Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty already pairs Taizu with Heaven at the suburban altar, as Zhou paired Hou Ji with Heaven; Taizong should therefore pair with the Lord at the Bright Hall, as Zhou paired King Wen.

sentences.zh: 仁宗皇祐二年，始行明堂合祭天地，並配祖宗，乃一時變禮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangyou under Renzong, the Bright Hall joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth was first performed, with the imperial ancestors as associates—a temporary change in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In Renzong's Huangyou reign, year 2, the court first performed a Bright Hall joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth with the ancestors as associates—a one-time ritual change.

sentences.zh: 至嘉祐七年，再行宗祀，已悟皇祐之非，乃罷配享，仍徹地示之位，故有去並侑煩文之詔。

translations.literal: By the seventh year of Jiayou, when the ancestral sacrifice was performed again, the court had already recognized the Huangyou error, abolished associate tablets, and also removed the Earth Lord's position—hence the edict to eliminate the cumbersome joint-accompaniment rites.
translations.idiomatic: By Jiayou year 7, when the ancestral rite was held again, the court had already seen the Huangyou arrangement as wrong, ended associate tablets, and removed Earth from the rite—hence the edict stripping away cumbersome joint-accompaniment forms.

sentences.zh: 如嘉祐之詔，則太祖地示已不與祭；

translations.literal: As the Jiayou edict shows, Taizu and the Earth Lord no longer shared the sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jiayou edict, Taizu and Earth no longer shared the altar;

sentences.zh: 元豐正祀典之詔，則悉罷群祀。

translations.literal: the Yuanfeng edict rectifying the sacrificial canon abolished miscellaneous sacrifices altogether.
translations.idiomatic: and the Yuanfeng edict reforming the sacrificial canon abolished miscellaneous rites entirely.

sentences.zh: 臣等謂將來明堂大饗，宜專祀昊天上帝，而以太宗配。」

translations.literal: We your subjects hold that at future Bright Hall great feasts, the Supreme Lord of the Vast Heaven alone should be worshipped, with Taizong as associate."
translations.idiomatic: We hold that future Bright Hall great feasts should worship the Supreme Lord of Heaven alone, with Taizong as associate."

sentences.zh: 後不果行。

translations.literal: This was not carried out in the end.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was never implemented.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，除大理卿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing he was appointed director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In 1132 he was made director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 宰相奏知平江府，帝曰：「誼，儒者，賴其奏讞平恕，使民不冤，勿令補外。」

translations.literal: The chief ministers memorialized to appoint him prefect of Pingjiang; the emperor said: "Zhang Yi is a Confucian scholar; we rely on his memorials on cases being fair and lenient so the people are not wronged—do not send him to an outside post."
translations.idiomatic: When the chief ministers proposed him as prefect of Pingjiang, the emperor said: "Yi is a scholar-official; we depend on his fair and measured case reports so the people are not wronged—do not post him outside the capital."

sentences.zh: 尋除權吏部侍郎，乞「詔有司編類四選通知之條，與一司專用之法，兼以前後續降指揮，自成一書。

translations.literal: Soon he was made acting vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and requested: "Order the relevant offices to compile the notification provisions of the four selection cycles together with the specialized regulations of each bureau, including successive directives issued before and after, into a single book.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting vice minister of Personnel and asked that the relevant offices compile the notification rules for all four selection cycles together with each bureau's specialized regulations and successive directives into one book.

sentences.zh: 如此則銓曹有可守之法，姦吏無舞文之弊，書成而吏銓有所執守矣。」

translations.literal: Thus the selection office would have statutes to uphold, corrupt clerks would have no loopholes for twisting the text, and once the book was complete the personnel bureau would have rules to follow."
translations.idiomatic: Then the selection office would have fixed rules to follow, corrupt clerks could not twist the text, and once the book was done the personnel bureau would have a standard to enforce."

sentences.zh: 改刑部侍郎兼詳定一司敕令，誼奏：「比修紹興敕令格式，其忠厚之意，則本於祖宗；

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of Justice with concurrent duty to review the unified bureau statutes; Zhang Yi memorialized: "In the recent revision of the Shaoxing statutes and formats, the spirit of generous fairness derives from the ancestors;
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to vice minister of Justice with concurrent duty reviewing the unified bureau statutes. Zhang Yi memorialized: "The recent Shaoxing statutes and formats preserve the generous spirit of the ancestors;

sentences.zh: 其綱條之舉，則仍於舊貫。

translations.literal: the main articles raised still follow the old practice.
translations.idiomatic: their main articles still follow established practice.

sentences.zh: 今在有司，為日既久，州縣推行，漸見牴牾。

translations.literal: Now that they have been in the offices for some time, as prefectures and counties implement them, contradictions gradually appear.
translations.idiomatic: But they have been in use long enough that implementation in the prefectures and counties is beginning to expose contradictions.

sentences.zh: 欲承疑遵用，則眾聽惑而不孚；

translations.literal: if one wishes to follow doubtful points in use, popular understanding is confused and not convinced;
translations.idiomatic: If officials follow doubtful passages as written, the public is confused and unconvinced;

sentences.zh: 欲因事申明，則法屢變而難守。

translations.literal: if one wishes to clarify matters case by case, the law changes repeatedly and is hard to uphold.
translations.idiomatic: if they clarify matters case by case, the law keeps changing and is hard to uphold.

sentences.zh: 乞詔監司、郡守與承用官司，參考祖宗舊典，各摭新書之闕遺，條具以聞，然後命官審訂刪去，著為定法。」

translations.literal: I beg that circuit commissioners, prefects, and the offices that apply the law be ordered, with reference to the ancestors' old canon, each to gather omissions and gaps in the new book, list them and report, and then officials be appointed to review, delete, and fix them as settled law."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that circuit commissioners, prefects, and applying offices consult the ancestors' canon, each gather gaps in the new code, report them in lists, and then have officials review, delete, and fix them as settled law."

sentences.zh: 遷徽猷閣直學士、樞密都承旨，誼奏：「漢有南北兩屯，唐有南北兩衛，皆天子自將之兵。

translations.literal: He was promoted to academician of the Huaiyou Pavilion and chief coordinator of the Bureau of Military Affairs; Zhang Yi memorialized: "Han had the northern and southern encampments; Tang had the northern and southern guards—all troops personally commanded by the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Huaiyou Pavilion academician and chief coordinator at the Bureau of Military Affairs. Zhang Yi memorialized: "Han had northern and southern encampments; Tang had northern and southern guards—all forces the emperor commanded in person.

sentences.zh: 祖宗所置殿班親軍，處禁門之內，皆極天下之選。

translations.literal: The palace guard and personal armies established by the ancestors, stationed inside the forbidden gates, were all the finest selections in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The palace guards and personal armies the ancestors placed inside the forbidden gates were drawn from the finest troops in the realm.

sentences.zh: 今日神武兵萃於五軍，多逃亡之餘，市井之人，殿班親軍，倚以侍衛者，曾無千百。

translations.literal: Today the Divine Martial troops are gathered in the five armies, mostly remnants of deserters and men of the marketplace; the palace guard and personal army on whom one relies for attendance and protection scarcely number one or two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Divine Martial forces are lumped into five armies filled with deserters and marketplace recruits; the palace guards on whom the throne relies for protection scarcely number a thousand or two.

sentences.zh: 願陛下酌漢、唐南北禁衛之意，修本朝遴選班直之法，選五軍及諸州各為一衛，合取萬人，分為兩衛，則禁衛增嚴，王室大競矣。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will consider the intent of Han and Tang's northern and southern forbidden guards, restore this dynasty's method of selecting palace guards, choose from the five armies and each prefecture one guard unit, gather ten thousand men in all, and divide them into two guards—then the forbidden guard will be strengthened and the royal house greatly secured."
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to take Han and Tang's northern and southern palace guards as a model, restore our method of selecting guards, draw one guard unit from each of the five armies and from each prefecture, gather ten thousand men, and split them into two guards—then the palace guard will be strengthened and the royal house greatly secured."

sentences.zh: 四年，金遣李永壽、王翊來，求還劉豫之俘，及西北人在東南者，又欲畫江以益劉豫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Jin sent Li Yongshou and Wang Yi, seeking return of Liu Yu's captives and northerners in the southeast, and also wishing to draw the river boundary to enlarge Liu Yu's domain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Jin sent Li Yongshou and Wang Yi to demand return of Liu Yu's captives and northerners held in the southeast, and also to redraw the Yangzi boundary in Liu Yu's favor.

sentences.zh: 時議難之，欲遣大臣為報使。

translations.literal: Court opinion found this difficult and wished to send a chief minister as envoy in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion resisted these demands, and ministers wanted to send a senior official as envoy in reply.

sentences.zh: 參政席益以母老辭，薦誼為代，加誼龍圖閣學士，充軍前奉表通問使，給事中孫近副之。

translations.literal: Vice Grand Councillor Xi Yi declined on grounds of an aged mother and recommended Zhang Yi as substitute; Zhang Yi was given the Dragon Diagram academician title and appointed envoy bearing the memorial before the armies for communication and inquiry, with Sun Jin, recipient of edicts, as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Grand Councillor Xi Yi declined because his mother was elderly and recommended Zhang Yi in his place. Yi was made Dragon Diagram academician and envoy bearing the memorial before the armies, with Sun Jin, recipient of edicts, as deputy.

sentences.zh: 誼至雲中，與粘罕、兀室論事，不少屈。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi reached Yunzhong and debated affairs with Nianhan and Wushi, yielding little.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi reached Yunzhong and debated with Nianhan and Wushi, conceding little.

sentences.zh: 金人諭亟還，誼曰：「萬里銜命，兼迎兩宮，必俟得請。」

translations.literal: The Jurchens urged him to return quickly; Zhang Yi said: "I have come ten thousand li on imperial commission, also to welcome the two palaces—I must wait until my request is granted."
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens pressed him to return at once. Zhang Yi replied: "I have come ten thousand li on imperial commission, also to welcome the two palaces—I must wait until my request is granted."

sentences.zh: 金人乃令蕭慶授書，併以風聞事責誼，誼詰其所自，金人以實告，乃還。

translations.literal: The Jurchens then had Xiao Qing deliver a letter and also reproached Zhang Yi on hearsay matters; Zhang Yi demanded where they came from, and the Jurchens told him the truth—then he returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens had Xiao Qing deliver a letter and also rebuked Zhang Yi on matters they had heard by rumor. Yi demanded their source; when they told him plainly, he returned.

sentences.zh: 至南京，劉豫留之，以計得歸。

translations.literal: When he reached Nanjing, Liu Yu detained him, but by stratagem he was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanjing, Liu Yu detained him, but Zhang Yi contrived his escape and returned.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉勞之，擢刑部尚書。

translations.literal: The emperor commended and rewarded him and promoted him to minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and rewarded him and promoted him to minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 是冬，帝親征，王師大捷于淮陰，誼扈從。

translations.literal: That winter the emperor campaigned in person; the imperial army won a great victory at Huaiyin, and Zhang Yi accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the emperor took the field in person; the imperial army won a great victory at Huaiyin, and Zhang Yi accompanied the campaign.

sentences.zh: 還臨安，遷戶部尚書，誼言：「祖宗設官理財，內則戶部，外則諸路轉運使、副，東南委輸最盛，則又置發運，以督諸路供輸之入，皆有移用補助之法，戶部仰以不乏者也。

translations.literal: On return to Lin'an he was moved to minister of Revenue; Zhang Yi said: "The ancestors established offices to manage finances: within, the Ministry of Revenue; without, the transport commissioners and deputies of each circuit. Where tribute from the southeast was greatest, they also established transport dispatch to supervise each circuit's deliveries inward—all had methods of transfer and supplementation on which the Ministry of Revenue relied so it would not be wanting.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Lin'an he was made minister of Revenue. Zhang Yi said: "The ancestors set up fiscal offices: the Revenue Ministry at court, transport commissioners and deputies in each circuit. Where southeastern tribute was heaviest they added transport dispatch to oversee deliveries—each with rules for transfers and supplements on which the ministry relied so funds would not run short.

sentences.zh: 今川、廣、荊湖土貢歲輸，不入王府者累年矣，皆發運使失職之罪也。

translations.literal: Now the annual local tribute deliveries from Sichuan, Guang, and Jinghu have for years not entered the imperial storehouse—all the fault of transport dispatch commissioners failing their duties.
translations.idiomatic: For years the annual tribute from Sichuan, Guang, and Jing-Hu has failed to reach the imperial treasury—all because transport dispatch commissioners have neglected their duties.

sentences.zh: 頃因定都汴京，故發運使置司真、泗，今駐吳會，則發運當在荊湖南、北之間。

translations.literal: Recently, because the capital was fixed at Bianjing, transport dispatch was stationed at Zhen and Si; now that the court resides in Wu region, transport dispatch should be between northern and southern Jinghu.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was at Bianjing, transport dispatch was based at Zhen and Si; now that the court is in the Wu region, its office should lie between northern and southern Jinghu.

sentences.zh: 望討論發運置司之地，選能臣以充其任。」

translations.literal: I hope the site for transport dispatch's office will be discussed and capable ministers chosen to fill the post."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the court decide where to base transport dispatch and choose able men for the post."

sentences.zh: 又言：「戶部左右曹之設，諸路運司則左曹之屬也，提舉則右曹之屬也。

translations.literal: He also said: "The establishment of the left and right sections in the Ministry of Revenue—the circuit transport commissioners are subordinate to the left section, and the intendant commissioners to the right.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "The Revenue Ministry's left and right sections correspond to circuit transport commissioners on the left and intendant commissioners on the right.

sentences.zh: 若復發運司，於諸路各置轉運使副二員，以一員檢察常平，以應右曹之選，則戶部財用無陷失矣。」

translations.literal: If transport dispatch is restored, and in each circuit two transport deputy commissioners are appointed, one to inspect the Ever-Normal Granaries to answer the right section's needs, then the Ministry of Revenue's finances will suffer no loss."
translations.idiomatic: If transport dispatch is restored and each circuit gets two transport deputies, one to inspect Ever-Normal Granaries for the right section, the ministry's finances will not be lost."

sentences.zh: 五年，以疾請郡，除龍圖閣學士、知溫州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, citing illness he requested a prefecture and was appointed Dragon Diagram academician and prefect of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he asked for a prefectural post on grounds of illness and was made Dragon Diagram academician and prefect of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 適歲大旱，米斗千錢，誼用劉晏招商之法，置場增直以糴，米商輻輳，其價自平。

translations.literal: Just then the year was severely drought-stricken and rice was a thousand cash per dou; Zhang Yi used Liu Yan's method of inviting merchants, set up markets and raised prices to purchase grain, rice merchants converged, and the price stabilized of itself.
translations.idiomatic: That year a severe drought drove rice to a thousand cash per dou. Zhang Yi used Liu Yan's method of inviting merchants, set up purchase stations at premium prices, merchants flocked in, and the price fell on its own.

sentences.zh: 部使者以狀聞，詔遷官一等。

translations.literal: The circuit commissioner reported the situation, and an edict advanced his rank one grade.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit commissioner reported this, and the court advanced his rank one grade.

sentences.zh: 六年，移守平江。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to guard Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 時將臨幸，供億繁夥，誼處之皆當於理。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to visit in person, supplies were numerous and complex; Zhang Yi handled them all appropriately.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to visit, the supply burden was heavy; Zhang Yi handled every item properly.

sentences.zh: 召對，賜帶笏，帝曰：「此不足以償卿之勞，其勿謝。」

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, he was granted belt and tablet; the emperor said: "This is not enough to repay your labors—do not thank me."
translations.idiomatic: Called to audience, he was granted belt and tablet. The emperor said: "This is not enough to repay your service—do not thank me."

sentences.zh: 明年，移蹕建康，復為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: The next year, when the court moved to Jiankang, he again became minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the court moved to Jiankang, he again became minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 誼奏營田之策，謂：「京西、湖北、淮南東西失業者最多，朝廷必欲家給牛種、人給錢糧以勸耕，則財力不足。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi memorialized on garrison-field policy, saying: "In Jingxi, Hubei, and eastern and western Huainan the unemployed are most numerous; if the court must give every household oxen and seed and every person cash and grain to encourage farming, fiscal strength is insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi memorialized on garrison farming, arguing that Jingxi, Hubei, and eastern and western Huainan had the most displaced people; if the court meant to give every household oxen and seed and every person cash and grain to encourage farming, the treasury could not bear it.

sentences.zh: 今三大將各屯一路，如各捐數縣地均給將士，收其餘以省轉輸，非小補也。」

translations.literal: Now the three great generals each garrison one circuit; if each donated several counties' land to distribute evenly among officers and soldiers, and the remainder were taken in to save transport costs, it would be no small supplement."
translations.idiomatic: The three great generals each hold a circuit; if each surrendered several counties' land to distribute among their troops and the surplus were kept to cut transport costs, that would be a substantial gain."

sentences.zh: 七年，帝還臨安，以誼為端明殿學士、江南東路安撫大使、知建康府兼行宮留守。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the emperor returned to Lin'an and appointed Zhang Yi academician of the Duanming Hall, grand pacification commissioner of Jiangnan East circuit, prefect of Jiankang, and concurrently keeper of the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the emperor returned to Lin'an and made Zhang Yi Duanming Hall academician, grand pacification commissioner of Jiangnan East, prefect of Jiankang, and keeper of the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 未幾，提舉毫州明道宮，代還。

translations.literal: Before long he was made superintendent of the Mingdao Palace in Bozhou and replaced on return.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made superintendent of the Mingdao Palace in Bozhou and relieved on his return.

sentences.zh: 八年卒，年六十一，諡「忠恪」。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died, aged sixty-one; his posthumous title was "Loyal and Respectful."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died at sixty-one; his posthumous title was Loyal and Respectful.

sentences.zh: 誼寬厚長者，故事，臺官言事，非挾怨以快己私，即用仇家言為人報復，誼獨存大體，士論歸之。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi was a generous and elder-like man. By precedent, when censors spoke on affairs, unless they bore private grudges to satisfy themselves, they used enemies' words to take revenge for others; Zhang Yi alone preserved the larger interest, and scholarly opinion approved him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi was generous and dignified. By precedent censors who did not act from private spite would use an enemy's testimony to settle scores for others; Zhang Yi alone kept the larger interest in view, and scholars approved him for it.

sentences.zh: 立朝論事，奏疏無慮數十百篇，皆經國濟時之策。

translations.literal: In court he debated affairs; his memorials numbered no fewer than several tens or hundreds, all policies to order the state and aid the age.
translations.idiomatic: In office he debated policy in memorials numbering well over a hundred, nearly all aimed at ordering the state and aiding the times.

sentences.zh: 初，席益薦誼使金，帝曰：「誼亦母老，朕當自諭之。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xi Yi recommended Zhang Yi as envoy to the Jin, the emperor said: "Zhang Yi also has an aged mother; I shall inform him myself."
translations.idiomatic: When Xi Yi first recommended Zhang Yi as envoy to the Jin, the emperor said: "Yi also has an elderly mother; I shall tell him myself."

sentences.zh: 誼聞命，略無難色，戒其家人勿使母知。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yi heard the order, he showed hardly any difficulty and warned his family not to let his mother know.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yi received the order he showed no reluctance and told his family not to let his mother know.

sentences.zh: 將行，告母曰：「是行不數月即歸，大似往年太學謁告時爾。」

translations.literal: About to depart, he told his mother: "This journey will return in no more than a few months, much like when I took leave from the Imperial Academy in former years."
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving he told his mother: "I will be back in a few months, much like when I took leave from the Imperial Academy in earlier years."

sentences.zh: 及還，母竟不知其使金也。

translations.literal: When he returned, his mother in the end did not know he had been envoy to the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, his mother never learned he had been envoy to the Jin.

sentences.zh: 誼卒，母年九十二。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yi died, his mother was ninety-two.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yi died, his mother was ninety-two.

sentences.zh: 子八人：駽、駒、駟、驔、𩤏、駉、馳、駰。

translations.literal: He had eight sons: Juan, Ju, Si, Zhan, (one character), Jiong, Chi, and Yin.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight sons: Juan, Ju, Si, Zhan, (one character), Jiong, Chi, and Yin.

sentences.zh: 韓肖胄

translations.literal: Han Xiaozhou
translations.idiomatic: Han Xiaozhou

sentences.zh: 韓肖胄，字似夫，相州安陽人。

translations.literal: Han Xiaozhou, courtesy name Sifu, was a native of Anyang in Xiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xiaozhou, whose courtesy name was Sifu, came from Anyang in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖琦，祖忠彥，再世為相。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Han Qi; his grandfather Han Zhongyan—two generations as chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather was Han Qi and his grandfather Han Zhongyan; for two generations his family had produced chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 父治。

translations.literal: His father was Han Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Han Zhi.

sentences.zh: 肖胄以蔭補承務郎，歷開封府司錄。

translations.literal: Xiaozhou entered office by yin privilege as clerk for ceremonial affairs and served as recorder of Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhou entered office by hereditary privilege as clerk for ceremonial affairs and served as recorder of the Kaifeng prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 與府尹同對殿中，徽宗問其家世，賜同上舍出身，除衛尉少卿，賜三品服。

translations.literal: He appeared in the hall together with the prefect; Huizong asked his family background, granted him upper-house student status, appointed him vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and bestowed third-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: He appeared at court with the prefect; Huizong asked about his lineage, granted him upper-house student status, made him vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and bestowed third-rank robes.

sentences.zh: 尋假給事中、充賀遼國生辰使。

translations.literal: Soon he was made acting recipient of edicts and appointed envoy to congratulate the Liao state on the imperial birthday.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made acting recipient of edicts and envoy to congratulate the Liao on the emperor's birthday.

sentences.zh: 既還，時治守相州，請祠。

translations.literal: After he returned, at the time Han Zhi was guarding Xiang prefecture and requested a temple post.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, his father Han Zhi was serving as prefect of Xiangzhou and had asked for a temple post.

sentences.zh: 肖胄因乞補外侍疾，詔除直秘閣、知相州，代其父任。

translations.literal: Xiaozhou therefore begged an outside appointment to attend to illness; an edict appointed him direct academician of the Secretariat and prefect of Xiang, replacing his father's post.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhou asked for an outside post to care for his father; the court made him a direct Secretariat academician and prefect of Xiangzhou, succeeding his father.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，帝曰：「先帝詔韓氏世官於相。

translations.literal: At his farewell audience the emperor said: "The late emperor decreed that the Han clan should hold office in Xiang generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience the emperor said: "The late emperor decreed that the Han family should hold office in Xiang generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 卿父子相代，榮事也。」

translations.literal: You and your father succeeding each other is a glorious matter."
translations.idiomatic: For father and son to succeed each other is a glorious thing."

sentences.zh: 在相四年，王師傳燕，肖胄策幽薊且有變，宜陰為守備。

translations.literal: During four years in Xiang, when imperial forces campaigned toward Yan, Xiaozhou judged that You and Ji would soon see trouble and that secret defensive preparations should be made.
translations.idiomatic: During his four years in Xiang, as imperial forces advanced toward Yan, Xiaozhou judged that the Yan region would soon see upheaval and urged quiet defensive preparations.

sentences.zh: 已而金騎入境，野無所掠而去。

translations.literal: Before long Jin cavalry entered the border; in the countryside they found nothing to plunder and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jin cavalry crossed the border, found nothing to plunder in the countryside, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，知江州，入為祠部郎，遷左司。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyan he was prefect of Jiang prefecture, entered the capital as director in the Ministry of Rites for sacrifices, and was moved to the left section.
translations.idiomatic: In 1128 he became prefect of Jiangzhou, entered the capital as a sacrifices director in the Rites Ministry, and was promoted to the left section.

sentences.zh: 嘗言：「中原未復，所恃長江之險，淮南實為屏蔽。

translations.literal: He once said: "The central plains are not yet recovered; what we rely on is the Yangzi's strategic barrier—Huainan is in truth our shield.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "The central plains are not yet recovered; we rely on the Yangzi barrier, and Huainan is our true shield.

sentences.zh: 沃野千里，近多荒廢，若廣修農事，則轉餉可省，兵食可足。」

translations.literal: Its fertile fields stretch a thousand li, but lately much lies waste; if farming is broadly restored, transport costs can be saved and military provisions made sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: Its fertile fields stretch a thousand li, but much has lately gone to waste; if farming is broadly restored, transport costs will fall and army rations will suffice."

sentences.zh: 自是置局建康，行屯田於江淮。

translations.literal: From this an office was established at Jiankang and garrison farming carried out on the Jiang and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter an office was set up at Jiankang and garrison farming was carried out on the Jiang and Huai.

sentences.zh: 又應詔陳五事，曰：遠斥堠，戢戍兵，防海道，援中原，修軍政。

translations.literal: He also responded to an edict with five proposals: extend outposts, restrain garrison troops, guard sea routes, aid the central plains, and reform military administration.
translations.idiomatic: He also answered an edict with five proposals: extend outposts, restrain garrison troops, guard sea routes, aid the central plains, and reform military administration.

sentences.zh: 擢工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時川、陝馬綱路通塞不常，肖胄請於廣西邕州置司，互市諸蕃馬，詔行之。

translations.literal: At the time the horse transport routes of Sichuan and Shaanxi were open or blocked without regularity; Xiaozhou requested that an office be established at Yong prefecture in Guangxi to trade with the various frontier peoples for horses, and an edict carried this out.
translations.idiomatic: Because Sichuan and Shaanxi horse routes were often blocked, Xiaozhou asked that an office be set up at Yongzhou in Guangxi to trade with frontier peoples for horses, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 時召侍從問戰守計，肖胄條奏千餘言，帝稱其所對事理簡當。

translations.literal: When attendants were summoned to discuss plans for war and defense, Xiaozhou memorialized in detail over a thousand words; the emperor praised his answers as concise and to the point.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor summoned attendants to discuss war and defense, Xiaozhou submitted a detailed memorial of more than a thousand words; the emperor praised his answers as concise and apt.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書席益歎曰：「援古證今，切于時用，非世官不能也。」

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Xi Yi sighed and said: "Drawing on antiquity to prove the present, pressing on timely use—only a hereditary official could do this."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Xi Yi sighed: "Citing antiquity to prove the present and pressing on what the times need—only a hereditary official could do that."

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，詔百官各言省費裕國、強兵息民之策，肖胄言：「天下財賦窠名，舊悉隸三司，今戶部惟有上供之目而已。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing an edict ordered all officials to speak on policies to save expense, enrich the state, strengthen the army, and give the people rest; Xiaozhou said: "The revenue categories of the realm formerly all belonged to the Three Bureaus; now the Ministry of Revenue has only the category of tribute deliveries to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 1132 an edict asked all officials for plans to save expense, enrich the state, strengthen the army, and give the people rest. Xiaozhou said: "Revenue categories once all belonged to the Three Bureaus; now the Revenue Ministry tracks only tribute to the capital.

sentences.zh: 問諸路窠名於戶部，戶部不能悉，問諸州窠名于漕司，漕司不能悉，失一窠名，則此項遂亡。

translations.literal: Ask the Ministry of Revenue about each circuit's categories and it cannot know them all; ask transport commissioners about each prefecture's categories and they cannot know them all—lose one category name and that item is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Ask the Revenue Ministry about each circuit's categories and it cannot list them all; ask transport commissioners about each prefecture's categories and they cannot either—lose one category name and that revenue stream vanishes.

sentences.zh: 願詔諸路漕司，括州縣出納，可罷罷之，可併併之，立為定籍。

translations.literal: I hope each circuit's transport commissioner will be ordered to tally prefectural and county receipts and disbursements, abolish what can be abolished, merge what can be merged, and fix them in a settled register.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that each circuit's transport commissioner tally prefectural and county receipts and disbursements, abolish what can be abolished, merge what can be merged, and fix them in a settled register.

sentences.zh: 漕司總諸州，戶部總諸路，則無失陷矣。

translations.literal: Let transport commissioners oversee the prefectures and the Ministry of Revenue oversee the circuits, and nothing will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Let transport commissioners oversee prefectures and the Revenue Ministry oversee circuits, and nothing will be lost.

sentences.zh: 經費之大，莫過養兵。

translations.literal: Of great expenditures, none surpasses maintaining the army.
translations.idiomatic: Of great expenditures, none surpasses maintaining the army.

sentences.zh: 今人亡而冒請者眾，願立諸軍核實之法，重將帥冒請之罪，則兵數得實，餉給不虛，省費裕國，此其大者。

translations.literal: Now many men are dead yet false claims abound; I hope methods of verifying each army will be established and generals' crime of false claiming heavily punished—then troop numbers will be true, rations not wasted, expense saved and the state enriched; this is the greatest matter.
translations.idiomatic: Many dead men still appear on the rolls; establish verification for each army and punish generals who file false claims—then troop numbers will be true, rations will not be wasted, and saving expense will enrich the state. This is the greatest matter.

sentences.zh: 生民常賦之外，迫以軍期，吏緣為姦，斂取百端。

translations.literal: Beyond the people's regular levies they are pressed by military deadlines; clerks use this to commit fraud and exact levies by a hundred means.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond regular taxes the people are pressed by military deadlines; clerks use this to commit fraud and exact levies by every means.

sentences.zh: 復為寇所迫逐，田桑失時，寇去復業，未及息肩，催科之吏已呼其門矣。

translations.literal: They are again driven by bandits; planting and sericulture miss their season; when bandits leave they return to farming, but before they can rest their shoulders, tax-collecting clerks are already at their doors.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits drive them off again; planting and sericulture miss their season; when bandits leave they return to the fields, but before they can catch their breath, tax collectors are already at their doors.

sentences.zh: 願詔郡邑，招集流散，官貸之種，俟及三年，始責其賦，置籍書之，以課殿最，強兵息民，此其先者。」

translations.literal: I hope prefectures and counties will be ordered to gather the displaced, lend them seed on official account, wait until three years have passed before levying their taxes, set up registers and record them, use this to grade performance—strengthen the army and give the people rest; this comes first."
translations.idiomatic: Order prefectures and counties to gather the displaced, lend them seed on official account, wait three years before levying taxes, keep registers, and grade officials on this basis—strengthen the army and give the people rest. This comes first."

sentences.zh: 時多所採納。

translations.literal: Many of his proposals were adopted at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 又請復天地、日月、星辰、社稷之祀，於是下有司定一歲祭禮。

translations.literal: He also requested restoration of sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, sun and moon, stars, and the altars of soil and grain; thereupon the relevant offices were ordered to fix the year's sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to restore sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, sun and moon, stars, and the altars of soil and grain; the relevant offices were then ordered to fix the year's sacrificial calendar.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎，時條例散失，吏因為姦，肖胄立重賞，俾各省記，編為條目，以次行之，舞文之弊始革。

translations.literal: He was moved to vice minister of Personnel; regulations were then scattered and lost, and clerks used this to commit fraud; Xiaozhou set heavy rewards, had each section record them, compiled them into articles, and implemented them in order—the abuse of twisting the text began to be reformed.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice minister of Personnel. Regulations were scattered and clerks exploited the gaps; Xiaozhou offered heavy rewards, had each section record them, compiled articles, and implemented them in order—abuses of twisting the text began to end.

sentences.zh: 陣亡補官，得占射差遣，而在部常調人，守待不能注授，且有短使重難。

translations.literal: Those who received offices for death in battle could seize priority assignments, while regular candidates in the ministry waited without appointment, and there were also light duties made heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Kin of men killed in battle could seize priority assignments, while regular candidates in the ministry waited without appointment, and light duties were sometimes made burdensome.

sentences.zh: 肖胄請陣亡惟許本家用恩例，異姓候經任收使，遂無不均，且嚴六部出入之禁，而請託不行。

translations.literal: Xiaozhou requested that for death in battle only the same surname might use the grace privilege, while different surnames must wait until they had served and been received—thus there was no inequality; he also tightened the six ministries' entry and exit restrictions so patronage requests could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhou asked that only same-surname kin of the fallen use grace appointments, while others must wait until they had served—ending unfairness. He also tightened entry rules at the six ministries so patronage requests could not succeed.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜端明殿學士、同簽書樞密院事，充通問使，以胡松年副之，肖胄慨然受命。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Duanming Hall academician and co-signer of the Bureau of Military Affairs, envoy for communication and inquiry, with Hu Songnian as deputy; Xiaozhou accepted the commission with resolve.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Duanming Hall academician and co-signer at the Bureau of Military Affairs, envoy for communication with the Jin, with Hu Songnian as deputy; Xiaozhou accepted with resolve.

sentences.zh: 時金酋粘罕專執政，方恃兵強，持和戰離合之策，行人皆危之。

translations.literal: At the time the Jin chief Nianhan monopolized government, relying on military strength and holding policies of alliance and war in alternation; envoys all regarded it as perilous.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin chief Nianhan then monopolized power, relied on military strength, and played alliance and war off against each other; every envoy regarded the mission as perilous.

sentences.zh: 肖胄入奏曰：「大臣各循己見，致和戰未有定論。

translations.literal: Xiaozhou entered and memorialized: "The chief ministers each follow their own views, so peace and war have no settled conclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhou memorialized: "Chief ministers each follow their own views, so peace and war have no settled conclusion.

sentences.zh: 然和乃權時之宜，他日國家安強，軍聲大振，誓當雪此仇恥。

translations.literal: Yet peace is a timely expedient; when another day the state is secure and strong and military renown greatly rises, we swear to wipe away this hatred and shame.
translations.idiomatic: Peace is only a timely expedient; when the state is secure and strong and military renown rises, we swear to wipe away this hatred and shame.

sentences.zh: 今臣等行，或半年不返命，必復有謀，宜速進兵，不可因臣等在彼而緩之也。」

translations.literal: Now that we your subjects depart, we may be half a year without returning with orders; there will surely be further plots—Your Majesty should advance troops quickly and must not slacken because we are there."
translations.idiomatic: We may be gone half a year without returning; there will surely be further plots. Your Majesty should advance troops quickly and must not slacken because we are there."

sentences.zh: 將行，母文語之曰：「汝家世受國恩，當受命即行，勿以我老為念。」

translations.literal: About to depart, his mother Lady Wen told him: "Your family has received the state's grace generation after generation; when you receive the order you must go at once—do not think of my old age."
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving, his mother Lady Wen told him: "Your family has received the state's grace for generations; when you receive the order, go at once—do not think of my old age."

sentences.zh: 帝稱為賢母，封榮國夫人。

translations.literal: The emperor called her a worthy mother and enfeoffed her as Lady of the Glorious State.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called her a worthy mother and enfeoffed her as Lady of the Glorious State.

sentences.zh: 肖胄至金國，金人知其家世，甚重之，往返才半年。

translations.literal: Xiaozhou reached the Jin state; the Jurchens knew his family background and treated him with great respect; the round trip took only half a year.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhou reached the Jin court; knowing his lineage, the Jurchens treated him with great respect, and the round trip took only half a year.

sentences.zh: 自帝即位，使者凡六七年未嘗報聘，至是始遣人偕來。

translations.literal: Since the emperor's accession, envoys for six or seven years had never been answered with a return mission—only now did they first send men to come together.
translations.idiomatic: Since the emperor's accession, envoys had gone six or seven years without a return mission—only now did the Jin first send envoys back with him.

sentences.zh: 肖胄先北使入對，與朱勝非議不合，力求去，以舊職知溫州，提舉臨安府洞霄宮。

translations.literal: Xiaozhou, having returned from the northern mission, entered audience; he disagreed with Zhu Shengfei and strongly sought to leave, taking his former rank as prefect of Wenzhou and superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace in Lin'an prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from the north, Xiaozhou had audience with the emperor, clashed with Zhu Shengfei, and pressed to leave office, becoming prefect of Wenzhou at his former rank and superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace in Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔問前宰執戰守方略，肖胄言：「女真等軍皆畏服西兵勁銳善戰，今三帥所統多西人，吳玠繼有捷奏，軍聲益振，敵意必搖，攻戰之利，臣固知之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year an edict asked former chief ministers for war and defense strategy; Xiaozhou said: "The Jurchen and other armies all fear and respect the western troops' strength, sharpness, and skill in battle; now the three commanders mostly lead westerners; Wu Jie has had successive victory reports; military renown rises further; enemy resolve must waver—the advantage of attack and battle, your subject already knows it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the court asked former chief ministers for war and defense strategy. Xiaozhou said: "Jurchen armies fear the western troops' strength and skill in battle. The three commanders mostly lead westerners; Wu Jie has reported successive victories; military renown is rising and enemy resolve must waver. I already know the advantage of giving battle.

sentences.zh: 自荊、襄至江、淮，綿亙數千里，不若擇文武臣僚按行計度，求險阻之地，屯兵積糧，則形勢相接。

translations.literal: From Jing and Xiang to the Jiang and Huai stretches several thousand li; better to choose civil and military officials to tour and plan, seek strategic terrain, station troops and store grain—then positions will link together.
translations.idiomatic: From Jing and Xiang to the Jiang and Huai the line runs several thousand li; better to send civil and military officials to survey the ground, find defensible positions, station troops, and store grain so the positions link together.

sentences.zh: 今淮東、西雖命宣撫使，然將屯置司，乃在江上，所遣偏裨分守，不過資以輕兵，勢孤力弱，難以責其固志。

translations.literal: Now eastern and western Huai have pacification commissioners appointed, yet the generals' encampments and offices are on the river; the subordinate commanders sent to divide defense are given only light troops—isolated and weak, it is hard to demand steadfast resolve of them.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern and western Huai have pacification commissioners, but generals' headquarters remain on the river; subordinate commanders posted to divide defense get only light troops—isolated and weak, they cannot be expected to hold firm.

sentences.zh: 當移二將於江北，使藩籬可固。」

translations.literal: The two generals should be moved to the north bank of the river so the barrier can be secured."
translations.idiomatic: Two generals should be moved to the north bank so the barrier can be secured."

sentences.zh: 又言：「諸大將之兵自主庭戶，更相仇疾。

translations.literal: He also said: "The great generals' troops are their own household guards and mutually hostile.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The great generals' troops are their own household guards and mutually hostile.

sentences.zh: 若欲並遣進攻，宜先命總帥，分以精銳，自成一軍，號令既一，則諸將疇敢不聽命。

translations.literal: If you wish to send them all forward in attack together, you should first appoint a supreme commander, assign elite troops, form a single army—once orders are unified, which general would dare not obey?
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to send them forward together, first appoint a supreme commander, assign elite troops, and form a single army—once orders are unified, which general would dare disobey?

sentences.zh: 畿甸、山東、關河之民怨金人入骨，當以安集流亡，招懷歸附為先，今淮南、江東西荒田至多，若招境上之人，授田給糧，捐其賦租，必將接跡而至。」

translations.literal: The people of the capital region, Shandong, and the passes and rivers hate the Jurchens to the bone; settling the displaced and winning those who return should come first. Now in eastern and western Huainan and Jiangdong there is much waste land; if people on the borders are invited, given land and grain, and their taxes remitted, they will surely come one after another."
translations.idiomatic: People of the capital region, Shandong, and the northern passes hate the Jurchens to the bone; settling the displaced and winning returnees must come first. Huainan and Jiangdong have much waste land; if border people are invited, given land and grain, and their taxes remitted, they will come in streams."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「江之南岸，曠土甚多，沿江大將各分地而屯，軍士舊為農者十之五六，擇其非甚精銳者，使之力耕，農隙則試所習之技藝，秋成則均以所種之禾麥，或募江北流徒及江南無業願遷之人分給之，創為營屯。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "South of the river there is much open land; the great generals along the river each divide territory and encamp; five or six tenths of the soldiers were formerly farmers—choose those not very elite, have them farm strenuously, in farming intervals drill the skills they know, at autumn harvest divide the grain and wheat they planted equally, or recruit refugees from north of the river and people in Jiangnan without livelihood who wish to move and distribute to them—establish garrison colonies.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "South of the river there is much open land. River generals each hold territory; five or six tenths of their soldiers were once farmers. Choose the less elite, put them to farming, drill skills in farming intervals, divide the harvest equally, recruit refugees from the north and landless people in Jiangnan willing to move, and establish garrison colonies.

sentences.zh: 止則固守，出則攻討。」

translations.literal: When they halt they hold firm; when they go out they attack."
translations.idiomatic: When they halt they hold firm; when they march out they attack."

sentences.zh: 起知常州，召赴行在，提舉萬壽觀，尋除簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was raised to prefect of Changzhou, summoned to the traveling palace, made superintendent of the Wanshou Abbey, and soon appointed signer of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Changzhou, summoned to the traveling palace, made superintendent of the Wanshou Abbey, and soon appointed signer at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 和議已定，復命肖胄為報謝使。

translations.literal: Once the peace agreement was settled, Xiaozhou was again appointed envoy of gratitude in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Once peace was settled, Xiaozhou was again appointed envoy of gratitude in reply.

sentences.zh: 接伴者逆於境，謂當稱謝恩使。

translations.literal: The reception envoy met him at the border and said he should be called envoy of gratitude for grace.
translations.idiomatic: The reception envoy met him at the border and said he should be called envoy of gratitude for grace.

sentences.zh: 肖胄論難三四反，遂語塞。

translations.literal: Xiaozhou debated three or four times and finally left him speechless.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhou debated three or four rounds and left him speechless.

sentences.zh: 既至，金遣人就館議事，肖胄隨問隨答，眾皆聳聽。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, the Jin sent men to the lodge to discuss affairs; Xiaozhou answered each question as it came, and all listened in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, the Jin sent men to the lodge to discuss affairs; Xiaozhou answered each question on the spot, and all listened in awe.

sentences.zh: 其還，給氈車及頓遞宴設，自肖胄始。

translations.literal: On his return he was given a felt carriage and relay banquets—beginning with Xiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was given a felt carriage and relay banquets—a courtesy that began with Xiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 除資政殿學士、知紹興府。

translations.literal: He was appointed academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance and prefect of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made academician of the Hall for Aid in Governance and prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 尋奉祠，與其弟膺胄寓居於越幾十年。

translations.literal: Soon he took a temple post and, with his younger brother Yingzhou, lived in retirement in Yue for nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he took a temple post and lived in retirement in Yue with his younger brother Yingzhou for nearly ten years.

sentences.zh: 事母以孝聞，弟不至不食，所得恩澤，皆先給宗族。

translations.literal: He was known for filial service to his mother; he would not eat until his brother arrived; favors he received he always gave first to the clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for filial devotion to his mother; he would not eat until his brother arrived; favors he received he always gave first to the clan.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十六，諡「元穆」。

translations.literal: He died, aged seventy-six; his posthumous title was "Original and Solemn."
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-six; his posthumous title was Original and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 琦守相，作晝錦堂，治作榮歸堂，肖胄又作榮事堂，三世守鄉郡，人以為榮。

translations.literal: When Qi guarded Xiang he built the Daytime Brocade Hall; when Zhi guarded it he built the Hall of Glorious Return; Xiaozhou again built the Hall of Glorious Affairs—three generations guarding their home prefecture, and people took it as honor.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi served in Xiang he built the Daytime Brocade Hall; when Zhi served there he built the Hall of Glorious Return; Xiaozhou built the Hall of Glorious Affairs—three generations guarding their home prefecture, and people counted it an honor.

sentences.zh: 陳公輔

translations.literal: Chen Gongfu
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gongfu

sentences.zh: 陳公輔，字國佐，台州臨海人。

translations.literal: Chen Gongfu, courtesy name Guozuo, was a native of Linhai in Tai prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gongfu, whose courtesy name was Guozuo, came from Linhai in Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 政和三年，上舍及第，調平江府教授。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenghe he passed the upper-house examination and was assigned instructor in Pingjiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1113 he passed the upper-house examination and was assigned instructor in Pingjiang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 朱勔方嬖幸，當官者奴事之，公輔絕不與交。

translations.literal: Zhu Mian was then a favorite; officials in office slaved for him, but Gongfu would have nothing to do with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mian was then a court favorite; officials fawned on him, but Gongfu would have nothing to do with him.

sentences.zh: 勔有兄喪，諸生欲往吊，公輔不予告。

translations.literal: When Mian had a brother's mourning, students wished to go to offer condolences; Gongfu would not grant leave.
translations.idiomatic: When Mian mourned a brother, students wished to attend the funeral; Gongfu refused them leave.

sentences.zh: 勔不悅，諷權要移公輔越州。

translations.literal: Mian was displeased and hinted to the powerful that Gongfu should be moved to Yue prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was displeased and hinted to the powerful that Gongfu should be transferred to Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷權應天府少尹，除秘書郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to acting vice prefect of Yingtian prefecture and appointed secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to acting vice prefect of Yingtian and was appointed a secretary.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，二府多宣和舊人，公輔言：「蔡京、王黼用事二十餘年，臺諫皆緣以進，唐重、師驥為太宰李邦彥引用，謝克家、孫覿為纂修蔡攸引用，及邦彥作相，又附麗以進。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang the two councils had many old men from the Xuanhe era; Gongfu said: "Cai Jing and Wang Fu held power for more than twenty years; censors and remonstrators all advanced by connection with them. Tang Zhong and Shi Ji were introduced by Grand Steward Li Bangyan; Xie Kejia and Sun Jue were introduced by compiler Cai You—and when Bangyan became chief minister, they attached themselves to advance again.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingkang reign the two councils were full of Xuanhe-era holdovers. Gongfu said: "Cai Jing and Wang Fu held power for more than twenty years; censors and remonstrators all advanced through them. Tang Zhong and Shi Ji were introduced by Grand Steward Li Bangyan; Xie Kejia and Sun Jue were introduced by compiler Cai You—and when Bangyan became chief minister, they attached themselves to advance again.

sentences.zh: 此四人者，處臺諫之任，臣知其決不能言宰相大臣之過。

translations.literal: These four men hold censor and remonstrator posts; your subject knows they certainly cannot speak of the faults of chief ministers and great officials.
translations.idiomatic: These four hold censor and remonstrator posts; I know they certainly cannot speak of chief ministers' faults.

sentences.zh: 願擇人臣中樸茂純直，能安貧守節、不附權幸、慷慨論事者，列之臺諫，則所任得人，禮義廉恥稍稍振起，敵國聞之，豈不畏服哉！」

translations.literal: I hope to choose among officials those who are plain, honest, and upright, who can be content in poverty and hold to integrity, who do not attach to the powerful and favored, who speak boldly on affairs—place them in censor and remonstrator posts, then the appointments will gain the right men, ritual, righteousness, integrity, and shame will gradually revive, and when enemy states hear of it, how would they not fear and submit!"
translations.idiomatic: Choose plain, honest officials who can live in poverty, hold to integrity, refuse the powerful, and speak boldly—place them in censor and remonstrator posts, and ritual, righteousness, integrity, and shame will gradually revive. When enemy states hear of it, how would they not fear and submit!

sentences.zh: 時吳敏、李綱不協，公輔奏：「陛下初臨萬機，正賴其同心合謀，而二臣不和，已有其跡，願諭以聖訓，俾務一心以安國家。」

translations.literal: At the time Wu Min and Li Gang were not in accord; Gongfu memorialized: "Your Majesty has just taken up the myriad affairs of state and rightly depends on their united hearts and combined counsel, yet the two ministers are not harmonious and signs of this already appear; I hope Your Majesty will instruct them with sacred teaching so they strive with one mind to secure the state."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Min and Li Gang were then at odds. Gongfu memorialized: "Your Majesty has just taken up rule and depends on their united counsel, yet these two ministers are already at odds. I hope Your Majesty will instruct them to strive with one mind to secure the state."

sentences.zh: 徽宗渡江未還，人情疑懼，公輔力陳父子之義，宜遣大臣迎奉。

translations.literal: Huizong had crossed the river and not returned; popular sentiment was doubtful and fearful; Gongfu strongly set forth the duty between father and son and urged that chief ministers be sent to welcome and escort him back.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong had crossed the Yangzi and not returned; the people were anxious. Gongfu strongly urged the duty between father and son and said chief ministers should be sent to welcome him back.

sentences.zh: 欽宗嘉之，擢為右司諫。

translations.literal: Qinzong commended him and promoted him to remonstrator of the right section.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzong commended him and made him remonstrator of the right section.

sentences.zh: 孟夏享景靈宮，遂幸陽德、佑神觀。

translations.literal: In early summer he sacrificed at the Jingling Palace, then visited the Yangde and Youshen abbeys.
translations.idiomatic: In early summer he sacrificed at the Jingling Palace, then visited the Yangde and Youshen abbeys.

sentences.zh: 公輔諫不當如平時事宴遊，論「蔡京父子懷姦誤國，終未行遣。

translations.literal: Gongfu remonstrated that he should not as in normal times pursue banquets and excursions, arguing: "The Cai Jing father and son harbored treachery and misled the state, yet in the end they were not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu remonstrated that the emperor should not pursue banquets and excursions as in normal times, arguing: "Cai Jing and his sons harbored treachery and misled the state, yet were never punished.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷公卿百執事半出其門，必有庇之者。」

translations.literal: Now half the court's chief ministers and officials came from their faction—there must be those who shield them."
translations.idiomatic: Now half the court's chief ministers and officials came from their faction—someone must be shielding them."

sentences.zh: 詔謫京崇信軍節度副使，德安府安置。

translations.literal: An edict banished Jing to vice military commissioner of Chongxin commandery, with residence assigned at De'an prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict banished Cai Jing to vice military commissioner of Chongxin and assigned him residence at De'an.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「朱勔罪惡，都城之民皆謂已族滅其家，乞勿許其子姓隨上皇入京。」

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Zhu Mian's crimes—the people of the capital all say his clan and household should be exterminated; I beg that his sons and kin not be allowed to follow the Retired Emperor into the capital."
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "Zhu Mian's crimes are such that the people of the capital say his whole clan should be exterminated; I beg that his sons and kin not be allowed to follow the Retired Emperor into the capital."

sentences.zh: 時有指公輔為李綱之黨，鼓唱士庶伏闕者。

translations.literal: At the time some accused Gongfu of being in Li Gang's faction and of inciting scholars and commoners to prostrate themselves before the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Some then accused Gongfu of belonging to Li Gang's faction and of inciting scholars and commoners to prostrate themselves before the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 公輔自列，因辭位，後陳三事：其一言李綱書生，不知軍旅，遣援太原，乃為大臣所陷，必敗事。

translations.literal: Gongfu stated the facts himself and therefore resigned his post; afterward he set forth three matters: first, that Li Gang was a scholar who did not understand military affairs—sending him to aid Taiyuan was a trap set by chief ministers and would surely fail.
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu stated the facts himself and resigned; afterward he set forth three matters: first, that Li Gang was a scholar who did not understand warfare—sending him to aid Taiyuan was a trap set by chief ministers and would surely fail.

sentences.zh: 其二言余應求不當以言遠謫。

translations.literal: Second, that Yu Yingqiu should not have been banished far for his words.
translations.idiomatic: Second, that Yu Yingqiu should not have been banished far for his words.

sentences.zh: 其三言方復祖宗法度，馮澥不宜更論熙寧、元豐之政。

translations.literal: Third, that as the ancestors' statutes were being restored, Feng Jie should not again discuss the policies of Xining and Yuanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Third, that as the ancestors' statutes were being restored, Feng Jie should not again discuss Xining and Yuanfeng policies.

sentences.zh: 語觸時宰，遂與應求、程瑀、李光俱得罪，斥監合州稅。

translations.literal: His words offended the chief minister of the time; he was then punished together with Yingqiu, Cheng Yu, and Li Guang, and demoted to supervise taxes in He prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His words offended the chief minister; he was punished together with Yingqiu, Cheng Yu, and Li Guang and demoted to supervise taxes in Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，召還，除尚書左司員外郎。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, Gongfu was recalled and appointed vice director of the left section in the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong took the throne, Gongfu was recalled and made vice director of the left section in the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，始達維揚。

translations.literal: The next year he finally reached Weiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he finally reached Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，李綱得政，公輔自外除郎，未至而綱罷，改南劍州，尋予宮觀。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Li Gang gained power, Gongfu was appointed director from outside but had not arrived before Gang was dismissed; he was changed to Nanjian prefecture and soon given a palace abbey post.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Gang first gained power, Gongfu was appointed from outside but had not arrived before Gang fell; he was sent to Nanjian and soon given a palace abbey post.

sentences.zh: 紹興六年，召為吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shaoxing he was recalled as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1136 he was recalled as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 疏言：

translations.literal: In a memorial he said:
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he said:

sentences.zh: 「今日之禍，實由公卿大夫無氣節忠義，不能維持天下國家，平時既無忠言直道，緩急詎肯伏節死義，豈非王安石學術壞之邪？

translations.literal: " Today's calamity is truly because chief ministers and great officials lack integrity and loyalty and cannot sustain the realm; in normal times they have no loyal words or straight paths—in crisis how would they die for principle? Is this not Wang Anshi's learning that ruined them?
translations.idiomatic: "Today's calamity comes because chief ministers lack integrity and loyalty and cannot sustain the realm. In normal times they offer no loyal counsel—in crisis how would they die for principle? Was this not ruined by Wang Anshi's learning?

sentences.zh: 議者尚謂安石政事雖不善，學術尚可取。

translations.literal: Discussants still say that though Anshi's administration was not good, his learning can still be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Critics still say that though Anshi's administration was bad, his learning can still be taken.

sentences.zh: 臣謂安石學術之不善，尤甚於政事，政事害人才，學術害人心，《三經》、《字說》詆誣聖人，破碎大道，非一端也。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that the badness of Anshi's learning is even worse than his administration—administration harms talent, learning harms hearts; the Three Classics and Explication of Characters slander the sages and shatter the great Way—not in one respect alone.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that Anshi's learning was worse than his administration—administration harmed talent, learning harmed hearts. The Three Classics and Explication of Characters slander the sages and shatter the great Way—not in one respect alone.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》正名分，定褒貶，俾亂臣賊子懼，安石使學者不治《春秋》；

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals rectify names and ranks, fix praise and blame, and make rebellious ministers and unfilial sons fear—Anshi had scholars not study the Spring and Autumn;
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals rectify names, fix praise and blame, and make traitors fear—Anshi had scholars stop studying them;

sentences.zh: 《史》、《漢》載成敗安危、存亡理亂，為聖君賢相、忠臣義士之龜鑑，安石使學者不讀《史》、《漢》。

translations.literal: the Records and Han Histories record success and failure, safety and peril, survival and ruin, order and chaos—as a tortoise mirror for sage rulers, worthy ministers, loyal subjects, and righteous men—Anshi had scholars not read the Records and Han Histories.
translations.idiomatic: the Records and Han Histories record success and failure, order and chaos—as a mirror for sage rulers and loyal subjects—Anshi had scholars stop reading them.

sentences.zh: 王莽之篡，揚雄不能死，又仕之，更為《劇秦美新》之文。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang usurped the throne, Yang Xiong could not die for principle but again served him and moreover wrote the "Exalting Qin and Praising Xin."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang usurped the throne, Yang Xiong could not die for principle but served him and wrote Exalting Qin and Praising Xin.

sentences.zh: 安石乃曰：『雄之仕，合於孔子無可無不可之義。』

translations.literal: Anshi then said: "Xiong's serving accorded with Confucius's doctrine of 'nothing that must be done, nothing that must not be done.'
translations.idiomatic: Anshi then said: "Xiong's serving accorded with Confucius's doctrine that one may do or not do as circumstances require."

sentences.zh: 五季之亂，馮道事四姓八君，安石乃曰：『道在五代時最善，避難以存身。』

translations.literal: In the chaos of the Five Dynasties, Feng Dao served four surnames and eight rulers; Anshi then said: "Dao in the Five Dynasties period was best—he avoided calamity to preserve his person.'
translations.idiomatic: In the chaos of the Five Dynasties, Feng Dao served four houses and eight rulers; Anshi said: "Dao in the Five Dynasties was best—he avoided calamity to preserve himself."

sentences.zh: 使公卿大夫皆師安石之言，宜其無氣節忠義也。」

translations.literal: If chief ministers and great officials all took Anshi's words as their teacher, it is fitting that they have no integrity or loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: If chief ministers all took Anshi as their teacher, it is fitting that they have no integrity or loyalty."

sentences.zh: 復授左司諫，言中興之治在得天得人，以孝感天，以誠得民。

translations.literal: He was again appointed remonstrator of the left section and said that restoration governance lies in gaining Heaven and gaining men—through filial piety move Heaven, through sincerity gain the people.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made remonstrator of the left section and said restoration governance lies in gaining Heaven and gaining men—through filial piety move Heaven, through sincerity gain the people.

sentences.zh: 帝善其深得諫臣體，賜三品服，令尚書省寫圖進入，以便觀覽。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him for deeply grasping the remonstrator's role, bestowed third-rank robes, and ordered the Ministry of State Affairs to copy his diagrams and submit them for convenient viewing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him for grasping the remonstrator's role, bestowed third-rank robes, and ordered the Ministry of State Affairs to copy his diagrams and submit them for review.

sentences.zh: 公輔感帝知遇，益罄忠鯁，言：「正心在務學，治國在用人，朝廷之禍在朋黨。」

translations.literal: Gongfu, moved by the emperor's recognition, gave his loyal candor ever more fully and said: "Rectifying the heart lies in devoting oneself to learning; governing the state lies in employing men; the court's calamity lies in factions."
