translations.idiomatic: Moved by the emperor's recognition, Gongfu gave his loyal candor ever more fully: "Rectifying the heart lies in learning; governing the state lies in employing men; the court's calamity lies in factions."

sentences.zh: 仍乞增輪對官，令審計、官告、糧料、榷貨、監倉及茶場等官，有己見，許面對。

translations.literal: He also begged to increase rotating audience officials and allow auditors, credential clerks, grain officers, monopoly officers, warehouse supervisors, and tea-yard officials who had their own views to be granted face-to-face audience.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to increase rotating audience officials and allow auditors, credential clerks, grain officers, monopoly officers, warehouse supervisors, and tea-yard officials who had views of their own to face the throne.

sentences.zh: 時有詔將駐蹕建康，公輔上疏陳攻守之策，且乞選大臣鎮淮西，增兵將守要害，使西連鄂、岳，東接楚、泗，皆有掎角之形。

translations.literal: At that time there was an edict that the court would establish its temporary residence at Jiankang. Chen Gongfu submitted a memorial setting forth strategies for offense and defense, and also requested that a senior minister be selected to command west of the Huai River, with increased troops and generals to guard strategic points, so that to the west it would link with Ezhou and Yuezhou and to the east connect with Chu and Si, forming a pincer formation throughout.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict announced that the court would take up residence at Jiankang, Chen Gongfu submitted a memorial outlining offensive and defensive strategy. He also asked that a senior minister be posted west of the Huai to reinforce troops at key positions, linking Ezhou and Yuezhou in the west with Chu and Si in the east so that the whole line would form a mutual pincer.

sentences.zh: 徽宗訃至，公輔請宮中行三年之喪，視朝服淡黃，群臣未可純吉服，明堂未當以徽宗配，宜罷臨軒策士。

translations.literal: When the news of Emperor Huizong's death arrived, Chen Gongfu requested that the three-year mourning be observed within the palace, that the emperor attend court in pale yellow robes, that the ministers not yet wear full auspicious mourning dress, that Emperor Huizong not yet be enshrined as associate at the Bright Hall, and that the imperial hall examination of scholars be cancelled.
translations.idiomatic: When word of Emperor Huizong's death arrived, Chen Gongfu urged that the court observe the full three-year mourning within the palace, that the emperor appear at court in pale yellow, that ministers not yet wear bright celebratory dress, that Huizong not yet be paired in the Bright Hall rites, and that the palace examination be suspended.

sentences.zh: 又乞權罷講筵，事不行。

translations.literal: He also requested that the lecture sessions be temporarily suspended; the proposal was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the imperial lecture hall be temporarily closed, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 會趙鼎言進退人才乃其職分，疏稍侵公輔，因力請祠。

translations.literal: When Zhao Ding said that promoting and dismissing talent was his proper duty, his memorial somewhat encroached on Chen Gongfu, who thereupon vigorously requested a temple appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Ding declared that appointing and removing officials was his own responsibility, his memorial took implicit aim at Chen Gongfu, who then pressed hard for a sinecure post at a Taoist temple.

sentences.zh: 除集英殿修撰、提舉江州太平觀，尋知處州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Talent and Director of the Taiping Temple in Jiangzhou, and soon afterward served as Prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Hanlin Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Talent and put in charge of the Taiping Temple in Jiangzhou, then shortly afterward became prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 升徽猷閣待制，乃提舉太平觀。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin Academician of the Huiyou Pavilion and then served as Director of the Taiping Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Hanlin Academician of the Huiyou Pavilion, he then took charge of the Taiping Temple.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六，贈太中大夫。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-six and was posthumously awarded the title Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-six and was posthumously ennobled as Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷，奏議十二卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He left twenty volumes of collected writings and twelve volumes of memorials, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty volumes of his collected writings and twelve volumes of memorials circulated after his death.

sentences.zh: 公輔論事剴切，疾惡如仇，惟不右程頤之學，士論惜之。

translations.literal: Chen Gongfu was incisive in discussing affairs and hated evil as if it were a personal enemy; only he did not support the learning of Cheng Yi, and scholars regretted this.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gongfu spoke to the point and hated wrongdoing with the passion of a sworn foe; his sole failing, in the eyes of literati opinion, was his refusal to champion Cheng Yi's school of thought.

sentences.zh: 張觷，字柔直，福州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xue, courtesy name Rouzhi, was a native of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xue, styled Rouzhi, came from Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為小官，不與世詭隨。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, served as a minor official, and did not follow the world's crooked ways.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he held a minor post and refused to bend with the times.

sentences.zh: 時蔡京當國，求善訓子弟者，觷適到部，京族子應之以觷薦，觷再三辭，不獲，遂即館，京亦未暇與之接。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing was in power, he sought someone skilled at instructing his sons. Zhang Xue happened to arrive at the department, and Cai Jing's clansman Yingzhi recommended Zhang. Zhang declined repeatedly but could not refuse, and so took up residence as tutor; Cai Jing also had no leisure to meet with him.
translations.idiomatic: While Cai Jing held power he looked for a tutor for his sons. Zhang Xue had just arrived in the capital when Cai's kinsman Yingzhi recommended him. Zhang tried several times to decline but could not; he moved into the household as tutor, though Cai Jing himself never found time to see him.

sentences.zh: 觷嚴毅聳拔，意度凝然，異于他師，諸生已不能堪，忽謂之曰：「汝曹曾學走乎？」

translations.literal: Zhang was stern, lofty, and grave in bearing, unlike other tutors, and the students already could not endure it. Suddenly he said to them, "Have you ever learned to run?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was austere and imposing, with a bearing quite unlike other tutors, and the boys were already at their limit. One day he suddenly asked them, "Have you ever been taught to run?"

sentences.zh: 諸生駭而問曰：「嘗聞先生教令讀書徐行，未聞教以走也。」

translations.literal: The students alarmed asked, "We have heard the Master teach us to read and walk slowly; we have never heard teaching to run."
translations.idiomatic: The boys were startled. "We have always been told to read and walk slowly," they said; "we have never been taught to run."

sentences.zh: 觷曰：「天下被而翁破壞至此，旦夕賊來，先至而家，汝曹惟有善走，庶可逃死爾。」

translations.literal: Zhang said, "The realm has been ruined to this point by your father; bandits will come any day and reach your home first—you can only hope to escape death by running well."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang replied, "Your father has brought the realm to ruin. Rebels will come any day, and your house will be the first hit. Your only hope of staying alive is to run fast."

sentences.zh: 諸子大驚，亟以所聞告京，曰：「先生心恙。」

translations.literal: The boys were greatly alarmed and quickly told Cai Jing what they had heard, saying, "The Master is mentally ill."
translations.idiomatic: The boys were terrified and rushed to tell Cai Jing that the tutor had lost his mind."

sentences.zh: 京矍然曰：「此非汝所知也。」

translations.literal: Cai Jing started and said, "This is not something you would understand."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing started. "That is not for you to understand," he said."

sentences.zh: 即見觷深語，觷慷慨言曰：「宗廟社稷，危在旦夕。」

translations.literal: He immediately went to see Zhang for a deep conversation, and Zhang spoke passionately, saying, "The altars of state are in peril at any moment."
translations.idiomatic: He went at once to speak privately with Zhang, who said with fierce urgency, "The altars of state stand on the edge of ruin."

sentences.zh: 京斂容問計，觷曰：「宜亟引耆德老成置諸左右，以開道上心。

translations.literal: Cai Jing composed himself and asked for a plan. Zhang said, "You should urgently bring in venerable elder statesmen and place them at your side, to open the sovereign's mind.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing collected himself and asked what should be done. Zhang said, "Summon respected elder statesmen at once and keep them close to the throne, so that the emperor's mind may be opened.

sentences.zh: 羅天下忠義之士，分佈內外，為第一義爾。」

translations.literal: Gather loyal and righteous men throughout the realm and distribute them inside and outside the court—this is the first priority."
translations.idiomatic: Gather loyal men from across the realm and deploy them throughout the court and the provinces—that must come first."

sentences.zh: 京因扣其所知，遂以楊時薦，於是召時。

translations.literal: Cai Jing pressed him for names he knew, and Zhang recommended Yang Shi; Yang was then summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing pressed him for names, and Zhang recommended Yang Shi, who was thereupon summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 觷後守南劍州，遷福建路轉運判官。

translations.literal: Later Zhang served as Prefect of Nanjian Prefecture and was transferred to Transport Commissioner for Fujian Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang later served as prefect of Nanjian and was promoted to transport commissioner for Fujian Circuit.

sentences.zh: 未行，會范汝為陷建州，遣葉徹擁眾寇南劍。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the post, Fan Ruwei seized Jianzhou and sent Ye Che with a crowd to raid Nanjian.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, Fan Ruwei captured Jianzhou and sent Ye Che at the head of a band to attack Nanjian.

sentences.zh: 時統制官任士安駐軍城西，不肯力戰，觷獨率州兵與之戰，分為數隊，令城中殺羊牛豕作肉串，仍多具飯。

translations.literal: At the time the commander Ren Shi'an had his army camped west of the city and refused to fight with full effort. Zhang alone led the prefectural troops to battle, dividing them into several companies and ordering the city to slaughter sheep, cattle, and pigs to make meat skewers while also preparing much food.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commander Ren Shi'an had his troops camped west of the city but would not fight hard. Zhang alone led the prefectural militia into battle. He divided them into several companies and had the city slaughter livestock for meat skewers while preparing large quantities of food.

sentences.zh: 將戰，則食第一隊人，既飽，遣之入陣，便食第二隊人，度所遣兵力將困，即遣第三隊人往代，第四至五六隊亦如之。

translations.literal: Before battle they fed the first company; once sated, they sent them into formation, then fed the second company. Estimating when the deployed force would grow weary, they sent the third company to replace them—the fourth through fifth or sixth companies likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Before each engagement he fed the first company; once they were full, he sent them into the line and fed the second. When he judged the men in the field near exhaustion, he sent the third company to relieve them, and did the same with the fourth, fifth, and sixth.

sentences.zh: 更迭交戰，士卒飽而力不乏。

translations.literal: They rotated in battle, and the soldiers were fed and their strength did not fail.
translations.idiomatic: By rotating companies in battle, his men stayed fed and never lost their strength.

sentences.zh: 徹中流矢死，眾敗走。

translations.literal: Ye Che was struck by an arrow and died, and the crowd fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Che was struck by an arrow and killed, and his followers fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 觷知士安懼無功，即函徹首與之，州兵皆憤，觷曰：「賊必再至，非與大軍合力不能破也。」

translations.literal: Zhang knew Ren Shi'an feared having no achievement to show, so he immediately boxed Ye Che's head and gave it to him. The prefectural troops were all indignant. Zhang said, "The bandits will surely come again; without joining forces with the main army we cannot defeat them."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Ren Shi'an feared returning without credit, Zhang boxed Ye Che's head and handed it over. The prefectural troops were furious, but Zhang said, "The rebels will come again. We cannot break them without the main army's help."

sentences.zh: 士安得之大喜，遂馳報諸司，謂已斬徹。

translations.literal: Ren Shi'an was greatly pleased upon receiving it and galloped to report to the various offices that he had already beheaded Ye Che.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Shi'an was delighted and galloped off to report to headquarters that he had personally beheaded Ye Che.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徹二子果引眾聲言復父仇，縞素來攻。

translations.literal: Before long, Ye Che's two sons indeed led a crowd, claiming to avenge their father, clad in white mourning to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Ye Che's two sons returned at the head of a force dressed in white mourning, crying that they would avenge their father.

sentences.zh: 於是士安與州兵夾攻，大敗之，城賴以全。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ren Shi'an and the prefectural troops attacked from both sides and routed them, and the city was thereby preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Shi'an and the prefectural troops then attacked from both sides and routed them, and the city was saved.

sentences.zh: 再知處州，嘗欲造大舟，幕僚不能計其直，觷教以造一小舟，量其尺寸，而十倍算之。

translations.literal: Serving again as Prefect of Chuzhou, he once wanted to build a large boat, but his staff could not calculate its cost. Zhang taught them to build a small boat, measure its dimensions, and multiply by ten to estimate.
translations.idiomatic: When he again served as prefect of Chuzhou, he once wanted to build a large vessel, but his staff could not estimate the cost. Zhang had them build a small boat, measure it, and multiply by ten.

sentences.zh: 又有欲築紹興園神廟垣，召匠計之，云費八萬緡，觷教之自築一丈長，約算之可直二萬，即以二萬與匠者。

translations.literal: Someone also wanted to build a wall for the Shaoxing Garden Spirit Temple. Craftsmen were summoned to estimate it and said it would cost eighty thousand strings of cash. Zhang taught them to build one zhang themselves, estimated it could cost twenty thousand, and gave the craftsmen twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When officials planned a wall for the spirit temple in the Shaoxing Garden, craftsmen quoted eighty thousand strings of cash. Zhang had them build one zhang of wall themselves, reckoned the true cost at twenty thousand, and paid the craftsmen that amount.

sentences.zh: 董役內官無所得，乃奏紹興空乏難濟，太后遂自出錢，費三十二萬緡。

translations.literal: The supervising eunuch got nothing from it and so memorialized that Shaoxing was empty and could not afford the work. The Empress Dowager then paid from her own funds, spending three hundred twenty thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch overseeing the project got nothing from the deal and reported that Shaoxing could not afford the work. The Empress Dowager then paid out of her own purse—three hundred twenty thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 以直龍圖閣知虔州，蕩平餘寇，進秘閣修撰，卒。

translations.literal: With appointment as Directly Attached to the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, he served as Prefect of Qianzhou, pacified the remaining bandits, was promoted to Secretariat Compiler, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed directly to the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, he governed Qianzhou, wiped out the remaining bandits, was promoted to Secretariat Compiler, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 後廟食邵武。

translations.literal: Later he was enshrined at a temple in Shaowu.
translations.idiomatic: He was later given a place in the temple at Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 胡松年

translations.literal: Hu Songnian
translations.idiomatic: Hu Songnian

sentences.zh: 胡松年，字茂老，海州懷仁人。

translations.literal: Hu Songnian, courtesy name Maolao, was from Huairen in Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Songnian, styled Maolao, came from Huairen in Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼孤貧，母粥機織，資給使學，讀書過目不忘，尤邃于《易》。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor in youth, his mother sold cloth woven on her loom to support his studies. When he read, he never forgot what he saw, and he was especially profound in the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor as a boy, he was supported by his mother's loom and cloth sales. He read with a photographic memory and was especially deep in the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 政和二年，上舍釋褐，補濰州教授。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenghe, upon graduation from the upper dormitory he entered service and was appointed Instructor at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenghe he graduated from the upper dormitory, entered official service, and was appointed instructor at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，賜對便殿，徽宗偉其狀貌，改校書郎兼資善堂贊讀。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was granted audience in the Privy Hall. Emperor Huizong admired his appearance and changed his appointment to Collator and Concurrent Reader at the Hall of Cultivating Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was granted audience in the Privy Hall. Emperor Huizong was impressed by his bearing and made him collator and concurrent reader at the Hall of Cultivating Virtue.

sentences.zh: 為殿試參詳官，以沈晦第一，徽宗大悅曰：「朕久聞晦名，今乃得之。」

translations.literal: As evaluation officer for the palace examination, he placed Shen Hui first. Emperor Huizong was greatly pleased and said, "I have long heard Shen Hui's name; now I have finally obtained him."
translations.idiomatic: Serving as evaluation officer for the palace examination, he ranked Shen Hui first. Emperor Huizong was delighted. "I have long known Shen Hui's name," he said; "now I have him at last."

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Drafting Officer of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to drafting officer of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時方有事燕雲，松年累章謂邊釁一開，有不勝言者。

translations.literal: At that time plans were underway for action in Yan-Yun. Hu Songnian repeatedly submitted memorials saying that once border conflict opened, the consequences would be unspeakable.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was preparing action in Yan-Yun, Hu Songnian submitted memorial after memorial warning that once border war began, the consequences would be beyond words.

sentences.zh: 咈時相意，提舉太平觀。

translations.literal: Going against the chief minister's intent, he was appointed Director of the Taiping Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Because he crossed the chief minister, he was sidelined as director of the Taiping Temple.

sentences.zh: 建炎間，密奏中原利害，召赴行在，出知平江府。

translations.literal: During the Jianyan era he secretly memorialized on the critical interests of the Central Plains, was summoned to the mobile court, and was appointed Prefect of Pingjiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianyan era he sent secret memorials on the strategic situation in the Central Plains, was summoned to the mobile court, and was sent out as prefect of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 未入境，貪吏解印斂跡，以興利除害十七事揭于都市，百姓便之。

translations.literal: Before he even entered the jurisdiction, corrupt officials resigned their seals and restrained themselves. He posted seventeen measures for promoting benefit and removing harm in the marketplace, and the people found them convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Before he even crossed the border of his jurisdiction, corrupt officials resigned and went to ground. He posted seventeen reforms for public benefit in the marketplace, and the people welcomed them.

sentences.zh: 加徽猷閣待制。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title Hanlin Academician of the Huiyou Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Hanlin Academician of the Huiyou Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 奏防江利害：一曰立國無藩籬之固，二曰遣將無首尾之援，三曰不攻敵技之所短。

translations.literal: He memorialized on Yangtze defense: first, establishing the state without solid barriers; second, dispatching generals without coordinated front-and-rear support; third, not attacking where the enemy's skills are weakest.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on Yangtze River defense with three points: the state lacked secure frontiers; dispatched generals lacked coordinated support; and the army failed to strike the enemy where it was weakest.

sentences.zh: 召為中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Drafting Officer of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as drafting officer of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 言武昌、九江、建昌、京口、吳江、錢塘、明、越宜各屯水戰士三千以為備。

translations.literal: He said that Wuchang, Jiujiang, Jianchang, Jingkou, Wujiang, Qiantang, Mingzhou, and Yuezhou should each station three thousand naval troops as a reserve.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that Wuchang, Jiujiang, Jianchang, Jingkou, Wujiang, Qiantang, Mingzhou, and Yuezhou each maintain three thousand naval troops as a reserve.

sentences.zh: 唐恪追復觀文殿學士，松年繳奏曰：「靖康之禍，何㮚輕脫寡謀，宜為罪首。

translations.literal: Tang Ke was posthumously restored as Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature. Hu Songnian returned the draft memorial, saying, "In the disaster of Jingkang, He Bi was rash, negligent, and lacking in planning—he should be counted chief among the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Ke was posthumously restored as Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, Hu Songnian returned the draft with a protest: "In the Jingkang catastrophe, He Bi was reckless and feckless. He should rank first among the guilty.

sentences.zh: 去年秦檜還朝，力稱其抗義守正，遂被褒贈，已大咈士論。

translations.literal: Last year when Qin Hui returned to court, he strongly praised Tang's righteous resistance and uprightness, and so Tang was honored posthumously—greatly against scholarly opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Last year, after Qin Hui returned to court and vigorously praised Tang's steadfast resistance, Tang was posthumously honored—a move that already outraged literati opinion.

sentences.zh: 今恪子琢自陳其父不獲伸迎請二帝之謀，飲藥而死。

translations.literal: Now Tang Ke's son Zhuo stated on his own behalf that his father was unable to carry out the plan to welcome back the two emperors and drank poison to die.
translations.idiomatic: Now Tang Ke's son Zhuo has declared that his father, unable to carry out a plan to bring the two captive emperors home, took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 此事凜然，追踪古人。

translations.literal: This matter is awe-inspiring and follows in the footsteps of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: The act is solemn and worthy, echoing the noblest examples of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 宜詔有司詳考實狀，庶不為虛美，以示激勸。」

translations.literal: The court should order the relevant offices to investigate the actual facts thoroughly, so that no empty praise is given, to show encouragement by example."
translations.idiomatic: The throne should order the proper offices to verify the facts, so that praise is not hollow and others may be moved to follow his example."

sentences.zh: 除給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 會選將帥，松年奏：「富貴者易為善，貧賤者難為功，在上之人識擢何如爾。

translations.literal: When generals were being selected, Hu Songnian memorialized, "The wealthy and noble find it easy to do good; the poor and lowly find it hard to achieve merit—it depends on how those above recognize and promote them.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was choosing generals, Hu Songnian wrote, "Wealth and rank make virtue easy; poverty makes achievement hard. Everything depends on whether those above know talent when they see it.

sentences.zh: 願陛下親出勞軍，即行伍搜簡之，必有可為時用者。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will personally go out to encourage the army and search among the ranks—there will surely be men usable in the time."
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to visit the camps in person and pick men from the ranks; there will surely be talent worth using."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「恢復中原，必自山東始，山東歸附，必自登、萊、密始，不特三郡民俗忠義，且有通、泰飛艘往來之便。」

translations.literal: He also memorialized, "Recovering the Central Plains must begin with Shandong; Shandong's allegiance must begin with Deng, Lai, and Mi—not only are the customs of those three prefectures loyal and righteous, but there is also the convenience of swift boats traveling between Tong and Tai."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote, "Recovering the Central Plains must begin in Shandong, and Shandong's loyalty must begin in Deng, Lai, and Mi. Those three prefectures are not only steadfast in custom, but also enjoy the advantage of fast boats running between Tongzhou and Taizhou."

sentences.zh: 除兼侍講。

translations.literal: He was appointed Concurrent Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made concurrent lecturer.

sentences.zh: 王倫使金還，言金人欲再遣重臣來計議，以松年試工部尚書為韓肖胄副，充大金奉表通問使。

translations.literal: Wang Lun returned from his mission to the Jin and said the Jurchens wished to send another high minister to discuss terms. Hu Songnian was tried as Minister of Works as deputy to Han Xiaozhou, serving as envoy bearing tables to the Great Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Lun returned from his mission to the Jin and reported that the Jurchens wanted another high minister for negotiations, Hu Songnian was appointed acting Minister of Works and deputy to Han Xiaozhou as envoy to the Great Jin.

sentences.zh: 時使命久不通，人皆疑懼，松年毅然而往。

translations.literal: At that time diplomatic missions had long been interrupted; all were fearful and doubtful, but Hu Songnian resolutely went.
translations.idiomatic: Diplomatic contact had long been broken off, and everyone was afraid, but Hu Songnian went resolutely nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 至汴京，劉豫令以臣禮見，肖胄未答，松年曰：「聖主萬壽。」

translations.literal: Arriving at Bianjing, Liu Yu ordered them received with the protocol due a subject. Han Xiaozhou did not reply. Hu Songnian said, "May the sage sovereign live ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: At Bianjing, Liu Yu required them to be received with the rites owed a subject. Han Xiaozhou said nothing, but Hu Songnian declared, "Long live the sage sovereign."

sentences.zh: 豫曰：「聖意何在？」

translations.literal: Liu Yu said, "Where lies the sage emperor's intent?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu asked, "What does the sage emperor intend?"

sentences.zh: 松年曰：「主上之意，必復故疆而後已。」

translations.literal: Hu Songnian said, "Our sovereign's intent is that the old territory must be recovered before he will stop."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Songnian replied, "Our sovereign will not rest until the old territory is recovered."

sentences.zh: 使還，拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Returning from the mission, he was appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 岳飛收復襄、漢，令松年籌度守禦事。

translations.literal: When Yue Fei recovered Xiang and Han, the court ordered Hu Songnian to plan defensive arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue Fei recovered Xiangyang and Hanzhong, the court put Hu Songnian in charge of planning the defense.

sentences.zh: 松年奏：「乞飛班師，徐窺劉豫意向，若豫置不問，其情叵測，當飭將士謹疆場可也。」

translations.literal: Hu Songnian memorialized, "I request that Yue Fei withdraw his army and observe Liu Yu's intentions slowly. If Liu Yu pays no attention, his intentions are unpredictable; the generals and soldiers should be ordered to guard the borders carefully."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Songnian urged that Yue Fei be recalled and Liu Yu's intentions watched closely. "If Liu Yu shows no reaction, his designs are unknowable," he wrote; "the troops should be ordered to hold the frontier with care."

sentences.zh: 又條戰艦四利：一曰張朝廷深入之軍勢，二曰固山東欲歸之民心，三曰震疊強敵，使不敢窺江、浙，四曰牽制劉豫不暇營襄、漢。

translations.literal: He also listed four benefits of warships: first, to display the court's depth of military power; second, to consolidate the hearts of Shandong people who wish to return; third, to shake the mighty enemy so they dare not probe Jiangsu and Zhejiang; fourth, to tie down Liu Yu so he has no leisure to operate in Xiang and Han.
translations.idiomatic: He also set out four advantages of a fleet: projecting the court's power deep into enemy territory; securing the loyalty of Shandong people who wish to return; overawing the enemy so they dare not threaten Jiangsu and Zhejiang; and pinning Liu Yu down so he cannot build strength in Xiang and Han.

sentences.zh: 除端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Academician of the Duanming Hall and Deputy Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Academician of the Duanming Hall and deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 首奏八事：「立規摹以定中興之基，振紀綱以尊朝廷之勢，馭將帥使知畏，撫士卒使知勸，收予奪之柄，察毀譽之言，無以小疵棄人才，無以虛文廢實效。」

translations.literal: He first memorialized eight matters: "Establish a plan to fix the foundation of restoration; strengthen discipline to honor the court's authority; control generals so they know fear; comfort soldiers so they know encouragement; recover the power to grant and withhold; examine words of praise and slander; do not discard talent over minor flaws; do not abandon real results for empty documents."
translations.idiomatic: His first memorial laid out eight priorities: set a blueprint for restoration; restore discipline to strengthen the throne; make generals fear disobedience and soldiers feel rewarded; reclaim the power of appointment and dismissal; weigh praise and slander carefully; reject no talent over small faults; and let no empty paperwork displace real achievement."

sentences.zh: 又薦張敵萬：「向在淮南誘敵深入，步騎四集，悉陷於淖，無得解者，金人至今膽落。

translations.literal: He also recommended Zhang Diwan: "Previously in Huainan he lured the enemy deep in; infantry and cavalry gathered on all sides and all sank in the mire with no escape—the Jurchens to this day have lost their courage.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended Zhang Diwan: "In Huainan he once lured the enemy deep into marshland until infantry and cavalry were trapped on every side with no escape. The Jurchens have never recovered their nerve.

sentences.zh: 乞令統率軍馬別為任使，庶幾外閫漸多名將，不獨仗倚三四人而已。」

translations.literal: I ask that he be given command of troops in a separate assignment, so that gradually many famous generals appear on the frontier, not relying on only three or four men."
translations.idiomatic: Give him an independent command, so that the frontier gradually gains more capable generals and the court is not reduced to leaning on three or four men alone."

sentences.zh: 諜報劉豫於登、萊、海、密具舟楫，淮陽、順昌積芻粟，欲憑藉金人侵我邊鄙。

translations.literal: Intelligence reported that Liu Yu had prepared boats at Deng, Lai, Hai, and Mi and stockpiled fodder and grain at Huaiyang and Shunchang, intending to rely on the Jurchens to invade our border regions.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence reported that Liu Yu was preparing boats at Deng, Lai, Hai, and Mi and stockpiling fodder and grain at Huaiyang and Shunchang, planning to use Jin support to raid the frontier.

sentences.zh: 議者謂韓、劉、岳各當一面，可保無虞。

translations.literal: Discussants said that Han, Liu, and Yue each holding one front could guarantee no worry.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that with Han Shizhong, Liu Guangshi, and Yue Fei each holding a front, there was nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 松年奏：「三人聲勢初不相屬，緩急必不相救。

translations.literal: Hu Songnian memorialized, "The three men's forces initially do not belong to each other; in urgency they will surely not rescue one another.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Songnian replied, "Those three commands are not linked. In a crisis they will not come to one another's aid.

sentences.zh: 況海道闊遠，蘇、秀、明、越最為要衝，乞選精兵萬人，命一大臣往駐建康，親督世忠、光世守採石、馬家渡，以張兩軍之勢，仍以兵五千屯明州、平江，控禦江海。

translations.literal: Moreover the sea route is broad and distant; Suzhou, Xiuzhou, Mingzhou, and Yuezhou are the most critical points. He requested selecting ten thousand elite troops and sending a senior minister to station at Jiankang, personally supervising Han Shizhong and Liu Guangshi guarding Caishi and Majiadu to expand the two armies' power, while also stationing five thousand troops at Mingzhou and Pingjiang to control the rivers and sea.
translations.idiomatic: The sea route is vast, and Suzhou, Xiuzhou, Mingzhou, and Yuezhou are the critical points. He asked for ten thousand picked troops and a senior minister posted at Jiankang to direct Han Shizhong and Liu Guangshi at Caishi and Majiadu, while five thousand men held Mingzhou and Pingjiang against attack from the rivers and sea.

sentences.zh: 或無人可遣，臣願疾馳以赴其急。」

translations.literal: If no one can be sent, I am willing to ride swiftly to answer the emergency."
translations.idiomatic: If no one else can be spared, I am willing to ride at once to meet the crisis."

sentences.zh: 詔遣松年往江上，與諸將會議進討，因覘賊情。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Hu Songnian to the Yangtze front to confer with the generals on advance and pursuit, and thereby observe enemy conditions.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Hu Songnian to the Yangtze front to confer with the generals on the advance and to reconnoiter the enemy.

sentences.zh: 帝決意親征，遂次平江，命松年權參知政事，專治戰艦，張浚專治軍器。

translations.literal: The Emperor resolved on a personal campaign and then halted at Pingjiang. He ordered Hu Songnian acting Vice Grand Councillor, specializing in warships, and Zhang Jun specializing in military equipment.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor resolved to take the field in person and halted at Pingjiang, he made Hu Songnian acting vice grand councillor in charge of warships and put Zhang Jun in charge of arms.

sentences.zh: 松年曰：「議論既定，力行乃有效，若今日行，明日止，徒紛紛無益。」

translations.literal: Hu Songnian said, "Once deliberation is settled, only forceful execution is effective. If you act today and stop tomorrow, it is merely chaotic and of no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Songnian said, "Once policy is settled, only steady execution counts. Start today and stop tomorrow, and nothing is gained but confusion."

sentences.zh: 俄以疾提舉洞霄宮，卜居陽羨，雖居閑不忘朝廷事，屢言和糴科斂、防秋利害，帝皆嘉納。

translations.literal: Soon, due to illness, he was appointed Director of the Dongxiao Palace and chose residence at Yangxian. Though living in retirement he did not forget court affairs, repeatedly speaking on the levy of grain under the hedi system and on autumn defense pros and cons, and the Emperor all praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon illness forced him to retire as director of the Dongxiao Palace at Yangxian. Even in retirement he kept advising the court on grain levies and autumn defense, and the emperor welcomed every memorial.

sentences.zh: 十六年，病革，呼其子曰：「大化推移，有所不免。」

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, critically ill, he called his son and said, "The great transformation shifts—some things cannot be avoided."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, on his deathbed, he called his son and said, "The great cycle turns; no one escapes it."

sentences.zh: 乃就枕，鼻息如雷，有頃卒，人謂不死也。

translations.literal: He then lay on his pillow; his breathing was like thunder. Shortly he died, and people thought he had not died.
translations.idiomatic: He lay back on his pillow, breathing like thunder. A moment later he was dead, yet for a time people thought he still lived.

sentences.zh: 年六十。

translations.literal: He was sixty years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty.

sentences.zh: 松年平生不喜蓄財，每除官例賜金帛，以軍興費廣，一無所陳請，或勸其白於朝，曰：「弗請則已，白之是沽名也。」

translations.literal: Hu Songnian throughout his life did not like to accumulate wealth. Each time he received an appointment he was customarily granted gold and silk, but because military expenses were vast he never requested any of it. Some urged him to inform the court, and he said, "If I do not request, that is enough; to inform the court would be seeking a reputation."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Songnian never cared to hoard wealth. Each promotion brought its customary grant of gold and silk, but with war costs soaring he never asked for a share. When others urged him to petition the throne, he said, "Not asking is enough; asking would be fishing for praise."

sentences.zh: 喜賓客，奉入不足以供費，或請節用為子孫計。

translations.literal: He enjoyed hosting guests, but his salary income was insufficient for the expense. Some urged him to economize for the sake of posterity.
translations.idiomatic: He loved entertaining guests, and his salary never covered the cost. Some urged him to cut back for his children's sake.

sentences.zh: 松年曰：「賢而多財，則損其志，況俸廩，主上所以養老臣也。」

translations.literal: Hu Songnian said, "If virtuous yet wealthy, ambition is harmed; moreover stipend is what the sovereign uses to support an old minister."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Songnian replied, "Wealth spoils a worthy man's resolve. Besides, my stipend is what the sovereign gives to sustain an old servant."

sentences.zh: 自持囊至執政，所舉自代，皆一時聞人，所薦一以至公，權勢莫能奪。

translations.literal: He personally carried his memorial pouch to the chief ministers. Those he recommended to succeed himself were all renowned men of the time, and his recommendations were utterly impartial—power and influence could not sway them.
translations.idiomatic: He carried his own recommendations to the chief ministers. Every man he proposed to succeed him was eminent, and no power or patronage could sway his choices.

sentences.zh: 方秦檜秉政，天下識與不識，率以疑忌置之死地，故士大夫無不曲意阿附為自安計。

translations.literal: While Qin Hui held power, all in the realm whether known to him or not were generally suspected and destroyed, so literati officials all without exception bent to flatter for self-preservation.
translations.idiomatic: While Qin Hui held power, anyone he knew or did not know could be destroyed by suspicion, so officials everywhere flattered him to survive.

sentences.zh: 松年獨鄙之，至死不通一書，世以此高之。

translations.literal: Hu Songnian alone despised this and until death exchanged not a single letter with him; the world esteemed him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Songnian alone scorned him and never exchanged a single letter with him to the day he died. The world honored him for it.

sentences.zh: 曹勛，字公顯，陽翟人。

translations.literal: Cao Xun, courtesy name Gongxian, was from Yangdi.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xun, styled Gongxian, came from Yangdi.

sentences.zh: 父組，宣和中，以閤門宣贊舍人為睿思殿應制，以占對開敏得幸。

translations.literal: His father Zu, during the Xuanhe era, as Gate Protocol Attendant served as Composer for the Hall of Sagacious Contemplation and gained favor through quick and clever divination responses.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zu, during the Xuanhe era, served as gate protocol attendant and composer for the Hall of Sagacious Contemplation, winning favor through his quick wit in divination and repartee.

sentences.zh: 勳用恩補承信郎，特命赴進士廷試，賜甲科，為武吏如故。

translations.literal: Cao Xun received appointment through privilege as Bearer of Faithful Trust, was specially ordered to take the palace jinshi examination, was granted top rank, and remained a military official as before.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xun entered service by privilege as Bearer of Faithful Trust, was specially ordered to sit the palace jinshi examination, received the highest rank, and remained a military officer.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，為閤門宣贊舍人、勾當龍德宮，除武義大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang he served as Gate Protocol Attendant and Supervisor of Longde Palace and was appointed Grand Master of Martial Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingkang era he was gate protocol attendant and supervisor of Longde Palace, and was made Grand Master of Martial Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 從徽宗北遷，過河十餘日，謂勛曰：「不知中原之民推戴康王否？」

translations.literal: Accompanying Emperor Huizong north, after crossing the river more than ten days, he said to Cao Xun, "I wonder whether the people of the Central Plains have enthroned Prince Kang?"
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying Emperor Huizong on the forced march north, more than ten days after crossing the river he asked Cao Xun, "Do you think the people of the Central Plains have rallied to Prince Kang?"

sentences.zh: 翌日，出御衣，書領中曰：「可便即真，來救父母。」

translations.literal: The next day he produced an imperial garment and wrote inside the collar, "You may immediately ascend the throne; come to rescue your parents."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he took out an imperial robe and wrote inside the collar, "Take the throne at once and come to save your parents."

sentences.zh: 並持韋賢妃、邢夫人信，命勛間行詣王。

translations.literal: He also held letters from Consort Wei and Lady Xing and ordered Cao Xun to travel secretly to reach the Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave Cao Xun letters from Consort Wei and Lady Xing and ordered him to make his way secretly to the prince.

sentences.zh: 又諭勛：「見康王第言有清中原之策，悉舉行之，毋以我為念。」

translations.literal: He further instructed Xun: "When you reach Prince Kang's residence, speak of strategies to recover the Central Plains; carry them all out completely; do not give thought to me."
translations.idiomatic: He also told Xun, "When you find Prince Kang, tell him of any plan to reclaim the Central Plains and put every part of it into action. Do not let concern for me hold you back."

sentences.zh: 又言藝祖有誓約藏之太廟，不殺大臣及言事官，違者不祥。

translations.literal: He also said that Emperor Taizu had a sworn oath stored in the Imperial Ancestral Temple: not to execute grand ministers or remonstrance officials; whoever violated it would meet ill fortune.
translations.idiomatic: He added that Taizu had left a sworn oath in the Imperial Ancestral Temple never to put to death grand ministers or officials who remonstrated; violation would bring ill fortune.

sentences.zh: 十一年，兀術遣使議和，授勛成州團練使，副劉光遠報之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Wuzhu sent envoys to negotiate peace; Xun was appointed Regimental Commissioner of Chengzhou and served as deputy to Liu Guangyuan in replying.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, Wuzhu dispatched envoys to discuss peace. Cao Xun was appointed Regimental Commissioner of Chengzhou and served as deputy to Liu Guangyuan in responding.

sentences.zh: 及淮，遇兀術，遣還，言當遣尊官右職持節而來，蓋欲亟和也。

translations.literal: When they reached the Huai, they met Wuzhu, who sent them back, saying a high-ranking official of senior rank bearing credentials should come—apparently because he wished to make peace quickly.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the Huai River, they met Wuzhu, who sent them home and said a senior official bearing imperial credentials should come instead—clearly eager to conclude peace at once.

sentences.zh: 勛還，遷忠州防禦使。

translations.literal: Xun returned and was transferred to Defender of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xun returned and was promoted to Defender of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 金使蕭毅等來，命勛為接伴使。

translations.literal: When Jin envoys Xiao Yi and others came, Xun was ordered to serve as reception commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin envoys led by Xiao Yi arrived, Cao Xun was appointed to receive them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，落階官為容州觀察使，充金國報謝副使，召入內殿，帝灑泣，諭以懇請親族之意。

translations.literal: Before long, stripped of rank-in-order he was made Observer of Rongzhou, appointed deputy envoy returning thanks to the Jin state; summoned into the inner hall, the Emperor wept and instructed him on the earnest wish to plead for kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given the honorary post of Observer of Rongzhou and appointed deputy envoy to return thanks to the Jin court. Summoned to the inner hall, the emperor wept and charged him with the earnest request to recover the imperial family.

sentences.zh: 及見金主，正使何鑄伏地不能言，勛反覆開諭，金主首肯許還梓宮及太后。

translations.literal: When they met the Jin ruler, chief envoy He Zhu prostrated himself unable to speak; Xun repeatedly explained and persuaded, and the Jin ruler nodded assent, promising return of the imperial coffin and the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: At their audience with the Jin emperor, chief envoy He Zhu fell prostrate and could not speak. Cao Xun argued the case again and again until the Jin ruler assented and agreed to return the imperial coffin and the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 勛歸，金遣高居安等衛送太后至臨安，命勛充接伴使。

translations.literal: Xun returned; the Jin sent Gao Ju'an and others to escort the Empress Dowager to Lin'an, and ordered Xun to serve as reception commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Xun returned, the Jin sent Gao Ju'an and others to escort the Empress Dowager to Lin'an and again appointed Xun to receive her.

sentences.zh: 遷保信軍承宣使、樞密副都承旨。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Bao Xin Army and Deputy Chief Palace Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Bao Xin Army and Deputy Chief Palace Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，拜昭信軍節度使，副王倫為稱謝使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he was appointed Military Commissioner of the Zhao Xin Army and served as deputy to Wang Lun as envoy of gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was made Military Commissioner of the Zhao Xin Army and served as deputy to Wang Lun on a mission of thanks.

sentences.zh: 時金主亮已定侵淮計，勛與倫還，言鄰國恭順，和好無他，人譏其妄。

translations.literal: At that time Jin ruler Hailing had already decided on a plan to invade the Huai region; Xun and Lun returned saying the neighboring state was deferential and the peace had no ulterior motive—people mocked their falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: By then Emperor Hailing of Jin had already settled on a plan to strike south across the Huai. When Cao Xun and Wang Lun returned, they reported that the neighbor was respectful and the alliance sound; people ridiculed their delusion.

sentences.zh: 孝宗朝加太尉、提舉皇城司、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaozong he was further made Grand Marshal, Commissioner of the Imperial City Bureau, and Grand Preceptor with the honors of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaozong he was further promoted to Grand Marshal, put in charge of the Imperial City Bureau, and granted the honors of Grand Preceptor equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 淳熙元年卒，贈少保。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunxi he died and was posthumously honored as Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of the Chunxi era and was posthumously granted the title Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 李稙，字元直，泗州臨淮人。

translations.literal: Li Zhi, courtesy name Yuanzhi, was a native of Linhuai in Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi, whose courtesy name was Yuanzhi, came from Linhuai in Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 幼明敏篤學，兩舉於鄉。

translations.literal: From youth he was bright and quick, devoted to learning, and twice passed the provincial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was bright and diligent in study, and twice passed the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 從父中行客蘇軾門，太史晁無咎見之曰：「此國士也。」

translations.literal: His father's younger brother Zhonghang was a guest in Su Shi's circle; Grand Astrologer Chao Wujiu saw him and said, "This is a man of national stature."
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Zhonghang moved in Su Shi's circle; when Grand Astrologer Chao Wujiu met Li Zhi he said, "Here is a man fit to serve the realm."

sentences.zh: 以女妻焉。

translations.literal: He gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Li Zhi his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，高宗以康王開大元帥府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang, Emperor Gaozong, as Prince Kang, established the Grand Marshal's Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingkang era, the future Gaozong, then Prince Kang, opened the Grand Marshal's Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 湖南向子諲轉運京畿，時群盜四起，餉道阨絕，環視左右無足遣者。

translations.literal: Xiang Ziyin of Hunan was transporting supplies to the capital region; at the time bandits rose everywhere, supply routes were cut off, and looking around him he had no one worth dispatching.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Ziyin of Hunan was moving supplies to the capital region. Bandits were rising on every side, supply lines were severed, and he found no one around him fit to send.

sentences.zh: 有以稙薦，遂借補迪功郎，使督四百艘，總押犒師銀百萬、糧百萬石，招募忠義二萬餘眾，自淮入徐趨濟，凡十餘戰，卒以計達。

translations.literal: Someone recommended Zhi; he was thereby given provisional appointment as Bearer of Merit, sent to supervise four hundred ships, overall escort of one million taels of silver for troop rewards and one million shi of grain, recruiting more than twenty thousand loyal volunteers, from the Huai entering Xu and hurrying to Ji, in all more than ten battles, finally reaching by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zhi was recommended, he received a provisional appointment as Bearer of Merit and was sent to supervise four hundred boats, escorting one million taels of silver in troop rewards and a million shi of grain while recruiting more than twenty thousand loyal volunteers. From the Huai he pushed through Xu toward Ji, fighting more than ten engagements, and finally broke through by stratagem.

sentences.zh: 時高宗駐師鉅野，聞東南一布衣統眾而至，士氣十倍，首加勞問。

translations.literal: At the time Gaozong was encamped at Juye; hearing that a commoner from the southeast leading troops had arrived, army morale was tenfold increased, and he first granted courteous inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong was then encamped at Juye. When he heard that a plain-clothed man from the southeast had arrived at the head of an army, morale surged tenfold, and he was the first to receive and commend him.

sentences.zh: 稙占對詳敏，高宗大悅，親賜之食，曰：「得一士如獲拱璧，豈特軍餉而已。」

translations.literal: Zhi answered in detail with nimble clarity; Gaozong was greatly pleased, personally bestowed food on him, and said, "To gain one such man is like obtaining a round jade disk—this is no mere matter of army provisions."
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi replied with detailed and nimble clarity. Gaozong was delighted, personally set food before him, and said, "To gain a man like this is like finding a treasured jade disk—not merely securing army supplies."

sentences.zh: 承制授承直郎，留之幕府。

translations.literal: By imperial order he was made Bearer of Upright Trust and kept in the headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: By special order he was made Bearer of Upright Trust and retained on the marshal's staff.

sentences.zh: 稙三上表勸進：「願蚤正大寶，以定人心，以應天意。」

translations.literal: Zhi thrice submitted memorials urging accession: "I wish that Your Majesty would early rightfully take the imperial throne, to settle the hearts of the people and respond to Heaven's intent."
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi submitted three memorials urging accession: "I pray that Your Majesty will soon take the throne in full right, to settle the people's hearts and answer Heaven's will."

sentences.zh: 三降手劄獎諭。

translations.literal: Three times the Emperor sent down handwritten notes of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Three times the emperor sent down handwritten notes of praise and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 稙感激知遇，言無不盡，為汪伯彥、黃潛善所忌。

translations.literal: Zhi, grateful for this favorable treatment, held nothing back in speech, and was resented by Wang Boyan and Huang Qianshan.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply moved by this favor, Li Zhi spoke his mind without reserve and was resented by Wang Boyan and Huang Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 高宗既即位，為東南發運司幹辦公事，尋以奉議郎知潭州湘陰。

translations.literal: After Gaozong had taken the throne, he served as staff officer of the Southeast Transport Commission; soon as Bearer of Discussion he was made magistrate of Xiangyin in Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong took the throne, Li Zhi served as a staff officer of the Southeast Transport Commission, and soon afterward was appointed magistrate of Xiangyin in Tanzhou with the rank Bearer of Discussion.

sentences.zh: 縣經楊么蕩析，稙披荊棘，立縣治，發廩粟，振困乏，專以撫摩為急。

translations.literal: The county had been ravaged by Yang Yao; Zhi cleared the brambles, established county administration, opened granary grain, relieved the distressed and impoverished, devoting himself chiefly to comfort and nurture.
translations.idiomatic: The county had been laid waste by Yang Yao. Li Zhi cut through the brambles, restored county government, opened the granaries, and relieved the destitute, making comfort and care his chief concern.

sentences.zh: 丞相張浚督師江上，知稙才，薦為朝奉郎、鄂州通判。

translations.literal: Grand councilor Zhang Jun supervised the army on the river; knowing Zhi's talent, he recommended him as Senior Gentleman of the Court and vice-prefect of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Zhang Jun was directing troops on the Yangzi. Recognizing Li Zhi's ability, he recommended him as Senior Gentleman of the Court and vice-prefect of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 大盜馬友、孔彥舟未平，稙請修戰艦，習水戰，分軍馬為左右翼，大破彥舟伏兵，誅馬友，二盜平。

translations.literal: Great bandits Ma You and Kong Yanchou were not yet pacified; Zhi requested repair of warships, drill in river fighting, divided troops and horses into left and right wings, greatly broke Yanchou's ambush, executed Ma You, and the two bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The great bandits Ma You and Kong Yanchou had not yet been subdued. Li Zhi had warships repaired, drilled his men in river fighting, and divided his forces into left and right wings. He smashed Yanchou's ambush, executed Ma You, and both bandits were brought to heel.

sentences.zh: 浚以破賊功上於朝，轉朝奉大夫、通判荊南府。

translations.literal: Jun reported the bandit-breaking achievement to the court; he was transferred to Grand Gentleman for Court Attendance and vice-prefect of Jingnan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun reported the victory to court, and Li Zhi was promoted to Grand Gentleman for Court Attendance and made vice-prefect of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，除尚書戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: When his term expired, he was appointed Outer Assistant Director in the Ministry of Revenue of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, he was appointed Outer Assistant Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時秦檜當國，凡帥府舊僚率皆屏黜，浚亦去國。

translations.literal: At the time Qin Hui controlled the state; generally all old staff of the Marshal's Headquarters were removed from office, and Jun also left the court.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui was then in power. Nearly all former staff of the marshal's headquarters were pushed aside, and Zhang Jun too left the court.

sentences.zh: 稙即丐祠奉親，寓居長沙之醴陵十有九年，杜門不仕。

translations.literal: Zhi immediately requested a sinecure to serve his parents, dwelt at Liling near Changsha for nineteen years, shut his doors and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi at once sought a sinecure so he could care for his parents, lived for nineteen years at Liling near Changsha, and kept his doors closed to office.

sentences.zh: 檜死，子諲以戶部尚書居邇列，語及龍飛舊事，識稙姓名，除戶部郎中。

translations.literal: When Hui died, Ziyin as Minister of Revenue was in the near ranks; speaking of the old events at the dragon's ascent he recognized Zhi's name, and Zhi was appointed Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin Hui died, Xiang Ziyin was Minister of Revenue and close to the throne. When talk turned to the old days of the emperor's accession, he remembered Li Zhi's name, and Li Zhi was appointed Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 稙始入見，帝曰：「朕故人也。」

translations.literal: When Zhi first entered audience, the Emperor said, "You are an old acquaintance of mine."
translations.idiomatic: On Li Zhi's first audience, the emperor said, "You are an old friend of mine."

sentences.zh: 方有意大用，以母老，每辭，願便養，除知桂陽軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to employ him greatly, but because his mother was aged, he repeatedly declined, wishing convenient nurture, and was appointed military prefect of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to give him great responsibility, but because his mother was old Li Zhi repeatedly declined, asking instead for a post that would let him care for her, and was appointed prefect of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，歸葬，哀毀廬墓，有白鷺朱草之祥。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother's death, returned to bury her, grieved with such destruction as to dwell by the tomb, and there were auspicious signs of white egrets and red grass.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he returned home to bury her, grieved so deeply that he lived in a hut by her tomb, and white egrets and red grass appeared as auspicious signs.

sentences.zh: 劉錡遺之書曰：「忠臣孝子，元直兼之矣。」

translations.literal: Liu Qi sent him a letter saying, "Loyal minister and filial son—Yuanzhi possesses both."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi wrote to him, "In loyalty and filial piety alike, Yuanzhi has both."

sentences.zh: 服闋，參政錢端禮薦差知瓊州。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Vice Administrator Qian Duanli recommended him for appointment as prefect of Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended, Vice Administrator Qian Duanli recommended him for appointment as prefect of Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，帝慨然曰：「卿老矣，瓊管遠在海外。」

translations.literal: On taking leave at court, the Emperor said with emotion, "You are old, and Qiong is far beyond the sea."
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience the emperor said with feeling, "You are old, and Qiongzhou lies far beyond the sea."

sentences.zh: 改知徽州。

translations.literal: He was changed to prefect of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as prefect of Huizhou instead.

sentences.zh: 徽俗崇尚淫祠，稙首以息邪說、正人心為事，民俗為變。

translations.literal: Huizhou custom revered illicit shrines; Zhi took as his first task ending heterodox teachings and rectifying hearts, and local customs changed.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhou's people favored illicit shrines. Li Zhi made suppressing heterodox cults and setting hearts right his first concern, and local customs changed.

sentences.zh: 轉朝請大夫、直秘閣，改知鎮江府，遷江淮荊湘都大提點坑冶鑄錢公事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Gentleman for Court Appearance and Direct Access to the Secret Archive, changed to prefect of Zhenjiang, and moved to overall intendant of mining, smelting, and coinage for the Jiang-Huai, Jing, and Xiang regions.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Gentleman for Court Appearance with direct access to the Secret Archive, reassigned as prefect of Zhenjiang, and then made overall intendant of mining, smelting, and coinage for the Jiang-Huai, Jing, and Xiang regions.

sentences.zh: 逾年，金人敗盟，朝廷將大舉，以稙漕運有才略，授直敷文閣、京西河北路計度轉運使。

translations.literal: After a year the Jin violated the treaty; the court was about to mount a major campaign; because Zhi had talent and strategy in transport, he was given Direct Access to the Hall of Spreading Culture and made transport commissioner for planning in the Jingxi and Hebei circuits.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the Jin broke the treaty and the court prepared a major campaign. Because Li Zhi showed talent and strategy in transport, he was given direct access to the Hall of Spreading Culture and appointed planning transport commissioner for the Jingxi and Hebei circuits.

sentences.zh: 稙措畫有方，廷議倚重。

translations.literal: Zhi arranged matters with method; court deliberations relied heavily on him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi planned with sound method, and court deliberations leaned heavily on him.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年，遷提刑江西。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiandao he was transferred to judicial intendant of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qiandao era he was made judicial intendant of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 二年，直寶文閣、江南東路轉運使兼知建康軍府兼本路安撫使，主管行宮留守司事。

translations.literal: In the second year: Direct Access to the Hall of Treasured Culture, transport commissioner of Jiangnan East circuit, concurrently prefect of Jiankang military prefecture and pacification commissioner of the circuit, in charge of affairs of the Traveling Palace Garrison Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was given direct access to the Hall of Treasured Culture, made transport commissioner of Jiangnan East circuit, concurrently prefect of Jiankang and pacification commissioner of the circuit, and put in charge of the traveling palace garrison headquarters.

sentences.zh: 稙上書極言防江十策，其略曰：「保荊、襄之障，以固本根；

translations.literal: Zhi submitted a memorial speaking exhaustively of ten strategies for defending the river; the gist was: "Protect the barrier of Jing and Xiang to solidify the root foundation;
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi submitted a memorial setting out ten strategies for river defense in detail. In summary he wrote: "Hold the barrier of Jing and Xiang to secure the state's foundation;

sentences.zh: 審中軍所處，以俟大舉；

translations.literal: Ascertain where the central army is placed, to await the major campaign;
translations.idiomatic: choose where the central army should stand, to await the great offensive;

sentences.zh: 搜選強壯，以重軍勢；

translations.literal: Search out and select the strong and robust, to reinforce military strength;
translations.idiomatic: recruit and select the strong to thicken the army's power;

sentences.zh: 度地險阨，以保居民；

translations.literal: Survey terrain's narrow passes and danger, to protect the inhabitants;
translations.idiomatic: survey defensible ground to protect the people;

sentences.zh: 避敵所長，擊其所短；

translations.literal: Avoid the enemy's strengths and strike his weaknesses;
translations.idiomatic: avoid what the enemy does best and strike where he is weak;

sentences.zh: 金人降者宜加賞勸。」

translations.literal: Jin men who surrender should be given increased rewards and encouragement."
translations.idiomatic: Jin deserters should be rewarded and encouraged."

sentences.zh: 皆直指事宜，不為浮泛。

translations.literal: All pointed directly at the affairs at hand, without floating vagueness.
translations.idiomatic: Every point went straight to practical matters, without empty generalities.

sentences.zh: 疏上，帝嘉其言，以太府卿召赴闕，有疾不克上道，遂以中奉大夫、寶文閣學士致仕，還湘。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor praised his words and summoned him to court as Minister of the Imperial Treasury; illness prevented his taking the road, and he therefore retired as Grand Gentleman for Palace Attendance and Academician of the Hall of Treasured Culture, returning to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor praised it and summoned him to court as Minister of the Imperial Treasury. Illness kept him from traveling, so he retired as Grand Gentleman for Palace Attendance and Academician of the Hall of Treasured Culture and returned to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 時胡安國父子家南嶽下，劉錡家湘潭，相與往還講論，言及國事，必憂形於色，始終以和議為恨。

translations.literal: At the time Hu Anguo and his sons lived below Mount Heng; Liu Qi lived in Xiangtan; they visited back and forth in discussion, and whenever they spoke of state affairs worry showed on their faces; from first to last they resented the peace negotiations.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Anguo and his sons lived below Mount Heng, and Liu Qi lived in Xiangtan. They visited one another in discussion, and whenever state affairs came up worry showed on their faces. To the end they regretted the peace settlement.

sentences.zh: 年七十有六，卒。

translations.literal: At age seventy-six he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷，題曰《臨淮集》，廬陵胡銓為之序。

translations.literal: He had a collected writings in ten juan, titled Collected Works of Linhuai, for which Hu Quan of Luling wrote the preface.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in ten juan titled Collected Works of Linhuai, with a preface by Hu Quan of Luling.

sentences.zh: 諡「忠襄」。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: "Loyal and Assisting."
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title "Loyal and Assisting."

sentences.zh: 子五人：汝虞，知桃源縣；

translations.literal: He had five sons: Ruyu, magistrate of Taoyuan county;
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Ruyu, magistrate of Taoyuan county;

sentences.zh: 汝士，朝奉大夫、知黃州；

translations.literal: Rushi, Senior Gentleman of the Court, prefect of Huangzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Rushi, Senior Gentleman of the Court and prefect of Huangzhou;

sentences.zh: 汝工，知昌化軍。

translations.literal: Rugong, military prefect of Changhua.
translations.idiomatic: and Rugong, prefect of Changhua.

sentences.zh: 韓公裔

translations.literal: Han Gongyi
translations.idiomatic: Han Gongyi

sentences.zh: 韓公裔，字子扆，開封人。

translations.literal: Han Gongyi, courtesy name Ziyi, was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gongyi, whose courtesy name was Ziyi, came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 初以三館吏補官，掌韋賢妃閣箋奏，尋充康王府內知客。

translations.literal: At first through service as a Three Halls clerk he received appointment, managed memorials for Consort Wei Xian's pavilion, and soon served as Inner Host of Prince Kang's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service as a clerk in the Three Halls, handled memorials for Consort Wei Xian's pavilion, and soon became inner host of Prince Kang's household.

sentences.zh: 金兵犯京，王出使，公裔從行。

translations.literal: When Jin troops invaded the capital, the Prince went on a mission, and Gongyi accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin troops attacked the capital, the prince went out on a mission and Gongyi went with him.

sentences.zh: 渡河，將官劉浩、吳湛私鬥，公裔諭之乃解。

translations.literal: Crossing the river, officers Liu Hao and Wu Zhan fought privately; Gongyi admonished them and they then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the river, officers Liu Hao and Wu Zhan fought among themselves; Gongyi reasoned with them until they stopped.

sentences.zh: 次磁州，軍民戕奉使王雲，隨王車入州廨，公裔復諭退之。

translations.literal: Stopping at Cizhou, soldiers and people killed envoy Wang Yun; they followed the Prince's carriage into the prefectural yamen; Gongyi again admonished them and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At Cizhou the soldiers and people killed the envoy Wang Yun and followed the prince's carriage into the prefectural yamen. Gongyi again reasoned with them until they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 王之將南也，與公裔謀，間道潛師夜起，遲明至相，磁人無知者，自是親愛愈篤。

translations.literal: When the Prince was about to go south, he plotted with Gongyi, took a byway with troops secretly marching by night, and at dawn reached Xiang; the people of Cizhou knew nothing—from then on affection grew ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was about to flee south, he and Gongyi planned a secret night march by a side road. At dawn they reached Xiangzhou without the people of Cizhou knowing. From then on the prince's affection for him deepened.

sentences.zh: 及兵退，張邦昌遣人同王舅韋淵來獻傳國璽。

translations.literal: When the troops withdrew, Zhang Bangchang sent men together with the Prince's maternal uncle Wei Yuan to present the imperial seal of transmission.
translations.idiomatic: After the armies withdrew, Zhang Bangchang sent men together with the prince's maternal uncle Wei Yuan to present the imperial seal of transmission.

sentences.zh: 時淵自稱偽官，議者又謂邦昌不可信，王怒將誅淵，公裔曰：「神器自歸，天命也。」

translations.literal: At the time Yuan styled himself an official of the false regime; debaters also said Bangchang could not be trusted; the Prince in anger was about to execute Yuan; Gongyi said, "The divine regalia returns of itself—this is Heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan then styled himself an official of the puppet regime, and others said Zhang Bangchang could not be trusted. The prince in anger was about to execute Yuan. Gongyi said, "The imperial regalia has returned of its own accord—this is Heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: 王遂受璽，命公裔掌之。

translations.literal: The Prince then accepted the seal and ordered Gongyi to keep charge of it.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then accepted the seal and put Gongyi in charge of it.

sentences.zh: 公裔力救淵，釋其罪。

translations.literal: Gongyi strenuously saved Yuan and released him from guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi pleaded hard for Yuan and secured his release from punishment.

sentences.zh: 元祐后詔王入承大統，府僚謂金兵尚近，宜屯彭城。

translations.literal: Empress Yuanyou ordered the Prince to enter and succeed to the great succession; headquarters staff said Jin troops were still near and he should encamp at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yuanyou ordered the prince to enter and succeed to the throne. The headquarters staff said Jin troops were still near and urged him to encamp at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 公裔言：「國家肇基睢陽，王亦宜於睢陽受命。」

translations.literal: Gongyi said: "The state was founded at Suiyang; the Prince also ought to receive the mandate at Suiyang."
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi said, "The dynasty was founded at Suiyang; the prince too ought to receive the mandate there."

sentences.zh: 時前軍已發，將趨彭城，會天大雷電，不能前，王異之，夜半抗聲語公裔曰：「明日如睢陽，決矣。」

translations.literal: At the time the vanguard had already set out and was about to head for Pengcheng; then heaven sent great thunder and lightning and they could not advance; the Prince thought it strange; at midnight he spoke loudly to Gongyi: "Tomorrow to Suiyang—decided."
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard had already set out toward Pengcheng when heaven sent thunder and lightning so violent that they could not advance. The prince took this as a sign. At midnight he spoke loudly to Gongyi: "Tomorrow we go to Suiyang—that is settled."

sentences.zh: 既即帝位，公裔累遷武功大夫、貴州防禦使。

translations.literal: After he had taken the throne, Gongyi was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Military Merit and Defender of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the prince took the throne, Gongyi was repeatedly promoted until he reached Grand Master of Military Merit and Defender of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 後以事忤黃潛善，適帝幸維揚，公裔丐去，潛善以為避事，遂降三官，送吏部。

translations.literal: Later because of a matter he offended Huang Qianshan; just as the Emperor was visiting Weiyang, Gongyi requested to leave; Qianshan took it as evading duty and therefore demoted him three ranks, sending him to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Later he gave offense to Huang Qianshan over some matter. When the emperor was visiting Yangzhou, Gongyi asked to leave office. Qianshan took this as shirking duty and had him demoted three ranks and sent to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝幸越，念其舊勞，召復故官、幹辦皇城司，仍帶御器械，累遷至廣州觀察使、提舉佑神觀。

translations.literal: When the Emperor visited Yue, remembering his old service, he summoned and restored his former office as staff officer of the Imperial City Bureau, still bearing imperial arms, and he was repeatedly promoted to Observer of Guangzhou and commissioner of the You Shen Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled to Yue, he remembered Gongyi's old service, recalled him to his former post as staff officer of the Imperial City Bureau, still bearing imperial arms, and eventually promoted him to Observer of Guangzhou and commissioner of the You Shen Abbey.

sentences.zh: 公裔給事藩邸三十餘年，恩寵優厚，每置酒慈寧宮，必召公裔。

translations.literal: Gongyi served the princely residence for more than thirty years with generous favor; whenever wine was set out in the Cining Palace, Gongyi was always summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi had served the princely household for more than thirty years with generous favor. Whenever the empress dowager held wine in the Cining Palace, Gongyi was always summoned.

sentences.zh: 會修《玉牒》，元帥府事多放佚，秦檜以公裔帥府舊人，奏令修書官就質其事。

translations.literal: When the Jade Register was being compiled, matters of the Marshal's Headquarters were much neglected; Qin Hui, because Gongyi was an old man of the headquarters, memorialized that the compilers should consult him on the events.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jade Register was being compiled, many events of the marshal's headquarters had been lost. Qin Hui, knowing Gongyi was an old member of that staff, memorialized that the compilers should consult him.

sentences.zh: 俄除保康軍承宣使，檜疑其舍己而求於帝，銜之。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Commissioner of the Bao Kang Army; Hui suspected he had bypassed him to seek favor from the Emperor and bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Commissioner of the Bao Kang Army. Qin Hui suspected he had gone over his head to the emperor and nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 右諫議大夫汪勃希檜意，劾罷公裔，遂與外祠，在外居住，而帝眷之不衰。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrance Grand Master Wang Bo hoping to please Hui impeached and dismissed Gongyi; he was then given an outside sinecure and lived externally, yet the Emperor's regard for him did not wane.
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrance Grand Master Wang Bo, eager to please Qin Hui, impeached and removed Gongyi. He was given an outside sinecure and lived away from court, yet the emperor's regard for him never faded.

sentences.zh: 檜死，即復提舉佑神觀，賜第和寧門西，帝曰：「朕與東朝欲常見卿，故以自近耳。」

translations.literal: When Hui died, he was immediately restored as commissioner of the You Shen Abbey and granted a residence west of the Henning Gate; the Emperor said, "The Empress Dowager and I wish often to see you, therefore we placed you nearby."
translations.idiomatic: After Qin Hui died he was at once restored as commissioner of the You Shen Abbey and given a residence west of the Henning Gate. The emperor said, "The empress dowager and I wish to see you often, so we have placed you close by."

sentences.zh: 升華容軍節度使，尋致仕。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Military Commissioner of the Hua Rong Army, and soon retired.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Military Commissioner of the Hua Rong Army and soon retired.

sentences.zh: 後華容軍復為岳陽軍，公裔遂換岳陽軍節度使。

translations.literal: Later when the Hua Rong Army was again renamed the Yue Yang Army, Gongyi accordingly exchanged to Military Commissioner of the Yue Yang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Hua Rong Army was renamed the Yue Yang Army, Gongyi exchanged his commission accordingly and became Military Commissioner of the Yue Yang Army.

sentences.zh: 高宗既內禪，嘗與孝宗語其忠勞，因詔所居郡善視之。

translations.literal: After Gaozong had abdicated in favor of a successor, he once spoke with Xiaozong of Gongyi's loyalty and service and thereby ordered the prefecture where he lived to treat him well.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong abdicated, he once told Xiaozong of Gongyi's loyal service and ordered the prefecture where he lived to look after him well.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年卒，年七十五，贈太尉，諡「恭榮」，官其親族八人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiandao he died at age seventy-five; posthumously honored as Grand Marshal, posthumous title "Respectful and Glorious," and eight of his kinsmen were given office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Qiandao era at seventy-five. He was posthumously made Grand Marshal, given the posthumous title "Respectful and Glorious," and eight of his kinsmen were granted office.

sentences.zh: 高宗賜金帛甚厚。

translations.literal: Gaozong bestowed gold and silk very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong bestowed gold and silk on him in great abundance.

sentences.zh: 公裔律身稍謹，不植勢，不市恩，又敢與黃潛善、秦檜異，斯亦足取云。

translations.literal: Gongyi regulated himself with some restraint, did not cultivate power, did not trade in favor, and also dared to differ from Huang Qianshan and Qin Hui—this too is worth noting.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyi kept himself in some measure of restraint, did not build a power base, did not trade in favors, and dared to stand apart from Huang Qianshan and Qin Hui—points in his favor as well.

sentences.zh: 論曰：章誼有蹇諤之節，肖胄席父祖之蔭，二人多所論建，奉使不辱，亦可取矣。

translations.literal: Commentary: Zhang Yi had the integrity of straightforward remonstrance; Xiao Zhou rested on the shade of father and grandfather; the two men made many proposals and constructions, and in foreign missions did not disgrace themselves—these too are admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Zhang Yi had the integrity of blunt remonstrance; Han Xiaozhou rested on the prestige of his forebears. Both offered many proposals and served abroad without disgrace—these are merits worth noting.

sentences.zh: 陳公輔得諫臣之體，其劾蔡京、王黼之黨，論吳敏、李綱之隙，是矣。

translations.literal: Chen Gongfu grasped the form of a remonstrance minister; his impeachment of the factions of Cai Jing and Wang Fu and his discussion of the rift between Wu Min and Li Gang were right.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gongfu understood what a remonstrance minister should be. His impeachment of the factions of Cai Jing and Wang Fu and his analysis of the breach between Wu Min and Li Gang were sound.

sentences.zh: 然既辨安石學術之害，而不尚程頤之學，何邪？

translations.literal: Yet having discerned the harm of Wang Anshi's learning, he did not esteem the learning of Cheng Yi—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet having seen the harm of Wang Anshi's doctrines, why did he not uphold the learning of Cheng Yi?

sentences.zh: 張觷斥蔡京之禍，薦楊時之賢，其趣操正矣，況平寇有術，而不自以為功乎？

translations.literal: Zhang Xue denounced the disaster of Cai Jing and recommended the worth of Yang Shi; his inclinations and conduct were upright; moreover he had method in pacifying bandits yet did not take credit for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xue condemned the ruin Cai Jing brought and recommended the worth of Yang Shi; his character was upright. Moreover, he had real skill in pacifying bandits yet did not claim the credit for himself.

sentences.zh: 松年鄙秦檜而不交，知命通方，固不易得。

translations.literal: Songnian despised Qin Hui and would not associate with him; understanding fate and mastering adaptability—this is indeed hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Songnian despised Qin Hui and would have nothing to do with him. To know one's fate yet remain adaptable—such men are not easily found.

sentences.zh: 而曹勛崎嶇兵間，稍著勞效，然金人入侵之計已決，猶曰鄰國恭順無他，何其見幾之不早邪？

translations.literal: Yet Cao Xun, toiling through the hardships of war, showed some merit; still, when the Jin plan to invade was already decided, he yet said the neighboring state was deferential with no ulterior motive—how late his foresight!
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xun endured the hardships of war and achieved some merit, yet when the Jin invasion was already decided he still reported that the neighbor was respectful and well disposed. How slow he was to read the signs!

sentences.zh: 若李稙、韓公裔早著忠藎，為天子故人，能與黃潛善、秦檜為異，閉門不出，待時而動，斯亦知所向方者哉！

translations.literal: As for Li Zhi and Han Gongyi, they early showed loyal devotion, were old acquaintances of the Son of Heaven, could differ from Huang Qianshan and Qin Hui, shut their doors and did not emerge, waiting for the time to act—these too knew which direction to face!
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi and Han Gongyi showed loyal devotion early on. As old companions of the emperor, they could stand apart from Huang Qianshan and Qin Hui, keep their doors closed, and wait for the right moment—they too knew where to stand.
